layout.style.title: LayoutStyle
layout.style.summary: Rules a parent uses to measure and place a widget: size, spacing, flex, grid, position, and overflow.
layout.style.section.overview.title: Overview
layout.style.section.overview.body:
Configure a widget's geometry using `widget.layout(style -> ...)`. Never manually calculate screen coordinates. Every size is a **request**: the parent container, flex/grid rules, and min/max constraints determine final bounds.

| Concept | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **Parent / Child** | The parent container measures and places widgets; children configure their layout behavior. |
| **Preferred Size** | Requested dimensions (`width`, `height`, `size`). May be clamped or redistributed by layout rules. |
| **`SizeValue.auto()`** | Automatically computes size from widget content or available space. Not synonymous with 100%. |
| **Main Axis** | Primary flex direction: width for `ROW`, height for `COLUMN`. |
| **Cross Axis** | Perpendicular axis to the main axis (height for `ROW`, width for `COLUMN`). |
| **Free Space** | Remaining space after placing base sizes and margins. Distributed via `flexGrow` and `flexShrink`. |

!!! warning "UniGUI Layout vs. Full Web CSS"
    While naming mirrors CSS properties, UniGUI implements a predictable, desktop-optimized layout engine. `PositionType.FIXED` is anchored relative to the nearest layout host (window or dialog), not the entire physical screen.
layout.style.section.size.title: Size and positioning
layout.style.section.size.body:
Request dimensions using `width`, `height`, `size`, or `sizePercent`. Dimensions can be specified in UI pixels, parent percentages, or `auto`. `minWidth` / `minHeight` and `maxWidth` / `maxHeight` enforce strict bounds.

| Method / Helper | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `width(w)` / `height(h)` | Dimensions | Sets width or height (`px`, `percent`, or `auto`). |
| `size(w, h)` | Shortcut | Sets both width and height in UI pixels simultaneously. |
| `sizePercent(w, h)` | Percentage | Requests percentages of the parent's available size. |
| `fixed(w, h)` | Fixed Bounds | Sets pixel size and disables flex growth and shrink (`0 0 auto`). |
| `fill()` | 100% Parent | Requests 100% width and 100% height (`sizePercent(100, 100)`). |
| `expand()` | Flex Remainder | Consumes remaining free space along the flex parent's **main axis** (`1 1 0px`). |
| `position(ABSOLUTE)` | Out-of-Flow | Removes widget from normal flow; position with `left`, `top`, `right`, `bottom`, or `inset`. |

!!! tip "Choosing between `fill()` and `expand()`"
    Use `fill()` when a widget must occupy 100% of both parent dimensions regardless of siblings.
    Use `expand()` when a flex child (such as a scrollable body) should absorb whatever free space remains after fixed elements (such as headers and footers).
layout.style.section.spacing.title: Spacing and overflow
layout.style.section.spacing.body:
Spacing governs margins around the widget, padding inside the border, and content clipping when elements exceed bounds.

| Spacing Property | Placement | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `margin(...)` | Exterior | Separates the widget from adjacent siblings without affecting internal layout. |
| `marginAutoHorizontal()` / `Vertical()` | Exterior | Absorbs available free space, centering or pushing the widget against edges. |
| `padding(...)` | Interior | Insets children away from the widget's outer boundary. |
| `gap(row, col)` | Between Items | Uniform or independent spacing between flex lines/items or grid tracks. |

| Overflow Mode | Visual Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `Overflow.VISIBLE` | Content renders beyond widget boundaries without clipping (default). |
| `Overflow.HIDDEN` | Content extending past boundaries is clipped. |
| `Overflow.AUTO` | Flags the axis as scrollable. Actual scrolling interactions are handled by `ScrollView`. |

!!! note "Scrolling Architecture"
    Setting `overflowY(Overflow.AUTO)` communicates intent to the layout engine, but scrolling interaction and scrollbars are provided by wrapping widgets in a `ScrollView`.
layout.style.section.flex.title: Flex layout
layout.style.section.flex.body:
Flexbox arranges children sequentially along a primary main axis (`ROW` or `COLUMN`).

### Container Configuration

| Property | Axis / Scope | Values | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `flexDirection` | Main Axis | `ROW`, `COLUMN`, `ROW_REVERSE`, `COLUMN_REVERSE` | Direction in which children are placed. |
| `flexWrap` | Wrapping | `NOWRAP`, `WRAP`, `WRAP_REVERSE` | Keeps children on one line or wraps to multiple lines. |
| `justifyContent` | **Main** Axis | `START`, `CENTER`, `END`, `SPACE_BETWEEN`, `SPACE_AROUND`, `SPACE_EVENLY` | Distributes children along the main axis. |
| `alignItems` | **Cross** Axis | `STRETCH`, `START`, `CENTER`, `END`, `BASELINE` | Aligns children perpendicular to the main axis. |
| `alignContent` | Multi-line | `START`, `CENTER`, `END`, `STRETCH`, `SPACE_BETWEEN` | Distributes wrapped lines (only active with `WRAP`). |
| `gap(row, col)` | Spacing | UI pixels (e.g. `gap(8.0f)`) | Space between items and between wrapped lines. |

### Child Item Weights & Presets

| Preset / Helper | Equivalent | Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `flexNone()` | `0 0 auto` | Rigid: keeps requested/content size; never grows or shrinks. |
| `expand()` | `1 1 0px` | Greedy: consumes all remaining free space on the parent's main axis. |
| `flexAuto()` | `1 1 auto` | Flexible: sizes to content, grows if space is free, shrinks if squeezed. |
| `flexInitial()` | `0 1 auto` | Shrink-only: keeps requested size, shrinks when crowded, does not grow. |
| `flex(grow, shrink, basis)` | Explicit | Custom weights for growth and shrinkage; `basis` is the starting size. |
| `alignSelf(Align)` | Override | Overrides parent's `alignItems` for this specific child. |
layout.style.section.grid.title: Grid and alignment
layout.style.section.grid.body:
Grid layout arranges widgets into a 2D matrix of columns and rows defined by `GridTrack` track specifications.

### Track Definitions (`GridTrack`)

| Track Builder | Type | Description | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `GridTrack.px(n)` | Fixed | Exact track size in UI pixels. | `GridTrack.px(96.0f)` |
| `GridTrack.fr(n)` | Fractional | Proportional share of leftover free space. | `GridTrack.fr(1.0f)` |
| `GridTrack.percent(n)` | Percentage | Percentage of the grid container's dimension. | `GridTrack.percent(33.3f)` |
| `GridTrack.auto()` | Automatic | Sized automatically to fit largest cell content. | `GridTrack.auto()` |
| `GridTrack.minmax(min, max)` | Constrained | Clamps track size within minimum and maximum limits. | `GridTrack.minmax(px(50), fr(1))` |

### Grid Properties & Placement

| Method | Target | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `gridTemplateColumns(...)` | Container | Explicit list of column tracks. |
| `gridTemplateRows(...)` | Container | Explicit list of row tracks. |
| `gridAutoColumns(...)` / `gridAutoRows(...)` | Container | Track sizes applied automatically beyond explicit templates. |
| `gridAutoFlow(GridAutoFlow)` | Container | Traversal direction for auto-placement: `ROW`, `COLUMN`, `ROW_DENSE`, `COLUMN_DENSE`. |
| `gridColumn(start, span)` | Child | 1-based column start index and span width (`<= 0` requests auto-placement). |
| `gridRow(start, span)` | Child | 1-based row start index and span height (`<= 0` requests auto-placement). |
| `alignSelf` / `centerSelf` | Child | Aligns this individual child inside its grid cell. |
| `zIndex(int)` | Child | Layering order among siblings (higher values render on top). |
layout.style.section.update.title: Batching and copies
layout.style.section.update.body:
A widget's live `LayoutStyle` automatically triggers layout reflow whenever a property changes. When applying several properties together, group mutations within `update(...)` to recalculate layout only once after the block finishes.

```java
style.update(s -> s
        .width(240.0f)
        .padding(12.0f)
        .flexNone());
```

| Lifecycle Method | Preserves Callback | When to Use |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `update(Consumer<LayoutStyle>)` | Yes | Batch multiple modifications; triggers exactly one recalculation. Safe to nest. |
| `copy()` | No | Creates a detached snapshot of all values with no widget callback attached. |
| `copyFrom(LayoutStyle other)` | Yes | Overwrites all property values from another style, keeping the existing owner callback. |

widget.base.title: WidgetBase
widget.base.summary: Shared widget foundation for layout, StylePack lookup, state, rendering, events, and animation.
widget.base.section.overview.title: Overview
widget.base.section.overview.body:
`WidgetBase` is the central abstract foundation for all UniGUI widgets. It unifies layout bounds, visual styles, input handling, invalidation tracking, focus traversal, transforms, animations, and render dispatch into a coherent fluent API.

| Core Subsystem | Primary Methods | Role & Architecture |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Hierarchy** | `parent()`, `children()`, `uiContext()` | Manages parent/child widget tree relations, layout measurement propagation, and contextual host access. |
| **Geometry & Layout** | `layout()`, `layoutStyle()`, `desiredSize()` | Measures and positions the widget via `LayoutStyle` (flexbox, CSS grid, margins, padding, size constraints). |
| **Visual Styling** | `style()`, `styleId()`, `styleClass()` | Handles inline CSS declarations, StylePack theme lookups, class selectors, and scoped style isolation. |
| **State & Interaction** | `visibility()`, `enabled()`, `mouseCursor()` | Governs layout flow participation, hover detection, custom mouse cursor, and tab focus management. |
| **Transforms & Animation** | `animate()`, `opacity()`, `rotationDegrees()` | Interpolates properties, executes FLIP layout transitions, spring physics, and multi-track storyboards. |
| **Rendering & Caching** | `renderer()`, `renderCached()`, `invalidate()` | Dispatches draw commands, supports retained render cache for leaf widgets, and manages dirty flags. |
| **Events** | `on()`, `emit()`, `handle()` | Strongly typed event listening and bubbling throughout the widget hierarchy. |

!!! note "Abstract Base Implementation"
    `WidgetBase` provides core infrastructure and is abstract. Build user interfaces using concrete built-in widgets (such as `Label`, `Button`, `VBox`, `ScrollView`) or extend it to implement custom controls.
widget.base.section.style.title: Style and layout
widget.base.section.style.body:
UniGUI cleanly separates **Layout** (geometry, positioning, and sizing) from **Style** (visual colors, borders, shadows, and textures).

| Styling Mechanism | Method / Syntax | Description & Behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Inline CSS Declarations** | `style("color: #fff; padding: 8px;")` | Parses property-value pairs into the widget's inline style. Parser warnings remain in `styleDiagnostics()`. |
| **StylePack Reference** | `styleId("card-primary")` | References a pre-defined theme style rule declared in an active `StylePack`. |
| **Style Classes** | `styleClass("btn primary")` / `addStyleClass("active")` | Assigns CSS classes for conditional or state-based styling rules (`:hover`, `:focused`, `:disabled`). |
| **Subtree Style Scope** | `styleScope(true)` | Isolates the widget subtree, preventing inherited styles from propagating beyond this boundary. |
| **Local Type Overrides** | `localStyle("Button", buttonStyle)` | Replaces the default style for all descendant widgets of the given type within this subtree. |
| **Layout Configuration** | `layout(style -> style.width(100).fill())` | Configures geometry via batched `LayoutStyle` callback, avoiding redundant layout invalidations. |

!!! tip "Performance Best Practice: Layout vs. Style"
    Mutating visual styles (e.g. changing `color` or `opacity`) only triggers a **VISUAL** invalidation (repaint). Changing geometry via `layout(...)` triggers a **LAYOUT** invalidation (remeasurement). Separating them ensures smooth 60+ FPS UI performance.
widget.base.section.state.title: Visibility, focus, and interaction
widget.base.section.state.body:
Widget visibility, user interactivity, and focus navigation are managed via explicit state flags.

| Visibility Mode | Layout Calculation | Visual Paint | Mouse / Input Events | Keyboard Focusable |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Visibility.VISIBLE` | Participates normally | Rendered | Receives events | Yes |
| `Visibility.HIDDEN` | Participates (preserves space) | Suppressed | Ignored | No |
| `Visibility.COLLAPSED` | Completely removed (zero size) | Suppressed | Ignored | No |

| Interaction Feature | Method | Purpose & Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Enablement** | `enabled(boolean)` | Enables or disables interaction. Inactive widgets receive the `:disabled` style pseudo-class and ignore events. |
| **Hover Query** | `hovered()` | Returns whether the cursor is currently within the widget's bounds. |
| **Custom Cursor** | `mouseCursor(MouseCursor)` | Sets active cursor shape (`HAND`, `TEXT`, `CROSSHAIR`, etc.) while enabled and visible. |
| **Focus Navigation** | `focusable(boolean)` | Enables tab navigation and keyboard focus for this widget. |
| **Focus Boundary** | `focusScope(true)` | Traps tab cycling within this widget's subtree (crucial for modal dialogs and dropdown menus). |
| **Tab Ordering** | `focusOrder(int)` | Explicit relative index for tab-key sequence ordering (default: document flow). |

!!! warning "Choosing `HIDDEN` vs. `COLLAPSED`"
    Use `Visibility.HIDDEN` when an element should temporarily vanish without causing sibling widgets to shift or recalculate positions. Use `Visibility.COLLAPSED` when the element should be removed from flow and yield its space.
widget.base.section.animation.title: Transforms and animation
widget.base.section.animation.body:
UniGUI provides a unified animation engine supporting instant transforms, interpolated transitions, spring physics, layout movement, and choreographies.

| Animation Technique | Method | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Direct Transform** | `opacity(val)`, `rotationDegrees(deg)`, `transformPivot(x, y)` | Instantly updates visual transform properties without animation overhead. |
| **Interpolated Transition** | `animate(property, target, spec)`, `animateOpacity(...)`, `animatePosition(...)`, `animateScale(...)` | Smoothly transitions a property using easing curves (`TransitionSpec`). In-flight transitions are smoothly retargeted. |
| **Spring Physics** | `animateSpring(property, target, stiffness, damping)` | Physically modeled damped harmonic oscillator motion with realistic bounce and overshoot. |
| **Layout Movement (FLIP)** | `layoutTransition(duration, easing)` | Animates positional changes caused by layout reflows using First-Last-Invert-Play (FLIP). |
| **Attention Feedback** | `shake(amplitude, duration)` | Oscillates the widget horizontally/vertically to indicate errors or invalid actions. |
| **Choreographed Storyboards** | `playStoryboard(storyboard)` | Complex, multi-target, multi-keyframe timelines managed by `StoryboardPlayer`. |

!!! note "Layout Transitions vs. Geometry Animation"
    `layoutTransition(...)` animates position displacement (X and Y coordinates) resulting from layout passes. It does not stretch or interpolate width/height dimensions.
widget.base.section.render.title: Rendering, invalidation, and events
widget.base.section.render.body:
The render pipeline separates layout measurement, visual draw command recording, and subtree invalidation.

| Invalidation Flag | Target Subsystem | When Triggered |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `InvalidationFlags.LAYOUT` | Layout Engine | Size, padding, margin, or flex rules changed. Propagates dirty flags upward to root. |
| `InvalidationFlags.VISUAL` | Render Pipeline | Colors, text, borders, or opacity changed. Triggers repaint without remeasuring geometry. |
| `InvalidationFlags.RETAINED_RENDER` | Draw Cache | Internal retained draw command cache invalidated. |

| Pipeline Component | Method | Purpose & Usage |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Custom Renderer** | `renderer(WidgetRender)` | Replaces the widget's default drawing commands with a custom procedural renderer. |
| **Retained Draw Cache** | `renderCachingEnabled(boolean)` | Records draw calls for static leaf widgets into a reusable buffer, drastically reducing GPU overhead. |
| **Event Subscription** | `on(EventType, listener)` | Registers a typed listener for input, focus, or lifecycle events. Returns an `EventSubscription` for unregistering. |
| **Event Dispatch** | `emit(Event)` | Dispatches a typed event directly to the widget and triggers listener callbacks. |

!!! important "Child Traversal with Custom Renderers"
    Assigning a custom `renderer(...)` replaces background and content rendering of the target widget. Child widgets belonging to the container are still traversed and drawn automatically by the framework.
widget.base.example.configure.title: Configure a widget
widget.base.example.configure.code:
Label greeting = new Label("Hello")
        .id("greeting")
        .styleId("card")
        .addStyleClass("interactive");

greeting.layout(style -> style
        .padding(12.0f)
        .width(240.0f)
        .flexNone());

layout.style.method.update.title: Batch updates
layout.style.method.update.summary: Applies several layout changes and notifies the owner once after the outer block finishes.
layout.style.method.update.markdown: Nested `update` calls are safe. The change callback runs only after the outermost block, and only if a property actually changed. A null consumer is ignored.
layout.style.method.update.parameter: Callback that mutates this style; null is a no-op.
layout.style.method.size.title: Set pixel size
layout.style.method.size.summary: Requests width and height in UI pixels. The legacy `LayoutConstraints.AUTO` value becomes `auto`.
layout.style.method.size.markdown: This is a size request, not a guaranteed final size. Flex, grid, min/max, and the parent can still change the result. It does not disable flex grow or shrink; use `fixed` for that.
layout.style.method.size.width: Width in UI pixels, or `LayoutConstraints.AUTO` for content-based sizing.
layout.style.method.size.height: Height in UI pixels, or `LayoutConstraints.AUTO` for content-based sizing.
layout.style.method.padding.title: Uniform padding
layout.style.method.padding.summary: Sets the same inner padding on all four sides, in UI pixels.
layout.style.method.padding.parameter: Padding applied to the left, top, right, and bottom edges.
layout.style.method.flex.title: Flex shorthand
layout.style.method.flex.summary: Sets grow weight, shrink weight, and the base size before free-space distribution.
layout.style.method.flex.markdown: Grow and shrink are weights, not percentages. `basis` is the starting main-axis size; `auto` uses the width or height request. The parent may still change the final size.
layout.style.method.flex.grow: Share of leftover main-axis space. `0` does not grow.
layout.style.method.flex.shrink: Share of the deficit when children do not fit. `0` does not shrink.
layout.style.method.flex.basis: Base main-axis size (`auto`, pixels, or percent). Null becomes `auto`.
layout.style.method.grid.columns.title: Grid columns
layout.style.method.grid.columns.summary: Sets the explicit column template. An empty or null list keeps automatic columns.
layout.style.method.grid.columns.markdow: Each `GridTrack` is one column: `px`, `percent`, `fr`, `auto`, or `minmax`. Tracks created beyond this template come from `gridAutoColumns`.
layout.style.method.grid.tracks: Column tracks in order. Null or an empty list clears the template.
layout.style.method.center.title: Center children
layout.style.method.center.summary: Centers the container's children on both the main and cross axes.
widget.base.method.style.title: Inline style
widget.base.method.style.summary: Applies inline declarations, or treats a bare token as a StylePack style id.
widget.base.method.style.markdown: A string without `:` or `;` is passed to `styleId`. Otherwise it is parsed as `property: value;` declarations and merged into the widget inline style. Parser diagnostics stay in `styleDiagnostics()`.
widget.base.method.style.parameter: Inline declarations, or a StylePack id when the string has no `:` or `;`.
widget.base.method.animate.title: Animate a property
widget.base.method.animate.summary: Transitions a built-in property to a target, or applies it immediately when duration is not positive.
widget.base.method.animate.markdown: A matching in-flight transition is retargeted instead of restarted. Rotation uses the shortest angle path. A null property is ignored; a null spec uses `TransitionSpec.DEFAULT`.
widget.base.method.animate.property: Built-in property such as opacity, position, scale, rotation, or pivot.
widget.base.method.animate.target: Target value. Opacity is clamped to 0..1; non-finite values are sanitized.
widget.base.method.animate.spec: Duration and easing. Null uses the default spec; non-positive duration snaps to the target.
widget.base.method.layout.title: Apply layout
widget.base.method.layout.summary: Updates the live `LayoutStyle` and batches the resulting layout invalidation.
widget.base.method.layout.parameter: Callback that mutates layout size, spacing, flex, grid, or position. Null is a no-op.
widget.base.method.visibility.title: Visibility
widget.base.method.visibility.summary: Sets whether the widget is shown, hidden in place, or removed from layout.
widget.base.method.visibility.markdown: `VISIBLE` participates in layout, rendering, input, and focus. `HIDDEN` keeps its layout space but skips rendering and input. `COLLAPSED` leaves the layout and invalidates both layout and visual state. Null becomes `VISIBLE`.
widget.base.method.renderer.title: Custom renderer
widget.base.method.renderer.summary: Replaces this widget's standard visual with one renderer instance.
widget.base.method.renderer.markdown: The renderer draws the widget background and content. Framework traversal still paints children. Null restores the standard visual. Style-declared renderers apply only when this slot is empty.
widget.base.method.renderer.parameter: Per-instance `WidgetRender`, or null for the standard visual.
widget.base.method.invalidate.title: Invalidate
widget.base.method.invalidate.summary: Marks layout or visual state dirty and bubbles the flags to ancestors.
widget.base.method.invalidate.markdown: Use `InvalidationFlags.LAYOUT` when measurement or placement changes, and `VISUAL` for a paint-only change. The call also dirties the retained render cache. `NONE` does nothing.
widget.base.method.invalidate.parameter: Bit flags from `InvalidationFlags`, usually `LAYOUT`, `VISUAL`, or both.
layout.style.method.position.title: Position mode
layout.style.method.position.summary: Selects normal-flow participation (RELATIVE/STATIC) or out-of-flow positioning (ABSOLUTE/FIXED).
layout.style.method.position.parameter: Positioning model; null normalizes to RELATIVE.
layout.style.method.width.sizevalue.summ: Requests desired width as auto, UI pixels, or a percentage of the parent.
layout.style.method.width.pixels.title: Set width in pixels
layout.style.method.width.pixels.summary: Requests desired width in UI pixels.
layout.style.method.width.parameter: Desired width; null normalizes to auto.
layout.style.method.width.pixels.paramet: Width in UI pixels, or AUTO for content-based sizing.
layout.style.method.height.sizevalue.sum: Requests desired height as auto, UI pixels, or a percentage of the parent.
layout.style.method.height.pixels.title: Set height in pixels
layout.style.method.height.pixels.summar: Requests desired height in UI pixels.
layout.style.method.height.parameter: Desired height; null normalizes to auto.
layout.style.method.height.pixels.parame: Height in UI pixels, or AUTO for content-based sizing.
layout.style.method.size.sizevalue.title: Set size (SizeValue)
layout.style.method.size.sizevalue.summa: Sets both width and height using SizeValue instances.
layout.style.method.sizepercent.title: Set size percent
layout.style.method.sizepercent.summary: Requests width and height as percentages of the parent container.
layout.style.method.fixed.title: Fixed size
layout.style.method.fixed.summary: Sets exact pixel width and height, completely disabling flex growth and shrinkage (0 0 auto).
layout.style.method.fill.title: Fill parent
layout.style.method.fill.summary: Requests 100% width and 100% height of the parent container.
layout.style.method.minwidth.title: Minimum width
layout.style.method.minwidth.summary: Sets the minimum allowable width to prevent unwanted collapsing.
layout.style.method.maxwidth.title: Maximum width
layout.style.method.maxwidth.summary: Sets the upper allowable width constraint.
layout.style.method.minheight.title: Minimum height
layout.style.method.maxheight.title: Maximum height
layout.style.method.maxheight.summary: Sets the upper allowable height constraint.
layout.style.method.inset.title: Edge insets
layout.style.method.inset.summary: Sets distances to all parent edges, typically used for ABSOLUTE positioning.
layout.style.method.margin.insets.title: Margin (EdgeInsets)
layout.style.method.margin.insets.summar: Sets exterior spacing separating the widget from siblings.
layout.style.method.margin.uniform.title: Uniform margin
layout.style.method.margin.uniform.summa: Sets the same exterior spacing on all four sides in UI pixels.
layout.style.method.margin.axes.title: Margin by axes
layout.style.method.margin.axes.summary: Sets horizontal and vertical exterior margins in UI pixels.
layout.style.method.margin.autoh.title: Auto horizontal margins
layout.style.method.margin.autoh.summary: Enables left and right auto-margins to absorb remaining horizontal space.
layout.style.method.margin.autov.title: Auto vertical margins
layout.style.method.margin.autov.summary: Enables top and bottom auto-margins to absorb remaining vertical space.
layout.style.method.padding.insets.title: Padding (EdgeInsets)
layout.style.method.padding.insets.summa: Sets interior spacing between widget boundaries and its children.
layout.style.method.padding.axes.title: Padding by axes
layout.style.method.padding.axes.summary: Sets horizontal and vertical inner paddings in UI pixels.
layout.style.method.overflowx.title: Horizontal overflow
layout.style.method.overflowx.summary: Controls content extending past the left and right boundaries (VISIBLE, HIDDEN, AUTO).
layout.style.method.overflowy.title: Vertical overflow
layout.style.method.overflowy.summary: Controls content extending past the top and bottom boundaries; scrolling handled by ScrollView.
layout.style.method.overflow.title: Uniform overflow
layout.style.method.overflow.summary: Sets overflow behavior simultaneously for both horizontal and vertical axes.
layout.style.method.flexdirection.title: Flex direction
layout.style.method.flexdirection.summar: Sets the main layout axis of the flex container (ROW or COLUMN).
layout.style.method.flexwrap.title: Flex wrap
layout.style.method.flexwrap.summary: Controls single-line (NOWRAP) vs multi-line (WRAP) item flow.
layout.style.method.flexwrap.parameter: Wrapping behavior when space runs out.
layout.style.method.flexflow.title: Flex flow
layout.style.method.flexflow.summary: Sets flex container direction and wrap mode together.
layout.style.method.gap.uniform.title: Uniform gap
layout.style.method.gap.uniform.summary: Sets uniform spacing between rows and between columns in UI pixels.
layout.style.method.gap.axes.title: Gap by axes
layout.style.method.gap.axes.summary: Sets row gap and column gap independently in UI pixels.
layout.style.method.flexnone.title: Flex none
layout.style.method.flexnone.summary: Disables flex growth and shrinkage, preserving exact requested/content size (0 0 auto).
layout.style.method.expand.title: Expand on main axis
layout.style.method.expand.summary: Greedily consumes all remaining free space along the flex parent's main axis (1 1 0px).
layout.style.method.flexauto.title: Flex auto
layout.style.method.flexauto.summary: Sizes widget from content, growing to absorb leftover space or shrinking if crowded (1 1 auto).
layout.style.method.flexinitial.title: Flex initial

draw.scope.title: DrawScope
draw.scope.summary: Safe draw-list facade for widget renderers that translates high-level drawing calls into backend-neutral commands, manages transform pivot adjustments, and provides zero-allocation immediate primitives.
draw.scope.section.overview.title: Architecture & Command Recording
draw.scope.section.overview.body:
`DrawScope` is the primary drawing facade provided to custom widget renderers (`WidgetRender#render(Widget, DrawScope)`). It bridges immediate-mode procedural rendering with UniGUI's deferred draw-list architecture.

Instead of issuing immediate OpenGL, Vulkan, or Direct3D state mutations, `DrawScope` translates each method invocation into an immutable `DrawCommand` appended to the frame's `DrawList`. This decoupled design enables automatic draw-call batching, multi-threaded rendering, retained display caching, and hardware-neutral compatibility across all supported platforms.

| Drawing Subsystem | Primary Methods | Capabilities & Architecture |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Standard Shapes** | `rect`, `roundedRect`, `circle`, `line`, `path` | High-level 2D geometric shapes styled using reusable `Paint` instances. |
| **Garbage-Free Primitives** | `rectFilled`, `rectStroke`, `circleFilled`, etc. | Zero-allocation drawing calls accepting raw `ColorView` parameters directly without creating temporary objects. |
| **Textures & Nine-Slice** | `texture`, `textureTinted`, `nineSlice` | Full-atlas UV mapping, rounded textures, and 9-slice expandable GUI panels. |
| **Text & Typography** | `text`, `addText` | Plain string and structured `RichText` typography with subpixel rasterization alignment. |
| **Direct Geometry & Meshes** | `addTriangle`, `addQuad`, `addMesh`, `ribbon` | Vertex-level arbitrary polygons, textured quads, custom indexed meshes, and procedural path ribbons. |
| **Vector Paths & Channels** | `pathLineTo`, `pathArcTo`, `pathBezier*`, `channelsSplit` | Interactive vector path construction and multi-channel draw-order layering. |
| **Clipping & Scissor** | `pushClip`, `pushTextClip`, `popClip` | Hardware-accelerated rectangular scissor regions with font-bleed compensation. |

!!! note "Immediate API, Deferred Execution"
    Calling drawing methods on `DrawScope` does not immediately render pixels to the screen. All commands are recorded in the active `RenderContext` and subsequently replayed, batched, and rendered by the active graphics backend.
draw.scope.section.transforms.title: Transforms & Pivot Anchoring
draw.scope.section.transforms.body:
When rendering custom widget graphics, child shapes and text must adhere to the widget's global transformations (translation, scale, rotation, skew, and pivot). `DrawScope` handles this coordination automatically.

### Automatic Pivot Adjustment (`transformFor`)

When a `DrawScope` is created with widget layout bounds (`transformBounds`), it calculates the relative offset between the widget's layout origin and each individual command's local coordinates.

```java
// Conceptual adjustment performed internally:
Transform adjusted = transform.copy();
adjusted.pivot().set(
        transform.pivot().x() + transformBoundsX - commandX,
        transform.pivot().y() + transformBoundsY - commandY);
```

This guarantees that all elements drawn inside the widget (such as background plates, icons, and text labels) rotate and scale as a unified visual unit around the widget's designated transform pivot, rather than rotating around their individual top-left coordinates.

### Nested Sub-Scopes

Use `withTransform(Transform)` to produce a lightweight child scope sharing the parent render context but applying a different local transformation (e.g. for spinning loading indicators or pulsating icons):

```java
DrawScope iconScope = scope.withTransform(spinningTransform);
iconScope.texture(iconTexture, 0, 0, 16, 16, paint);
```
draw.scope.section.primitives.title: Garbage-Free Drawing Primitives
draw.scope.section.primitives.body:
In high-performance Minecraft rendering running at 60 to 144+ FPS, allocating temporary objects during procedural drawing triggers frequent garbage collection pauses.

`DrawScope` provides two complementary drawing paradigms:

1. **Standard `Paint`-based Overloads (`rect`, `circle`, etc.)**: Convenient when styling parameters (fill, stroke, shader, filter) are encapsulated inside a reusable, cached `Paint` instance.
2. **Garbage-Free Overloads (`rectFilled`, `rectStroke`, `circleFilled`, etc.)**: Accept primitive float coordinates and `ColorView` instances directly. In standard UI rendering, these methods perform **zero heap allocations** per frame.

| Operation | Standard (Paint) | Garbage-Free (ColorView) | Allocation Impact |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Solid Rectangle** | `scope.rect(x, y, w, h, paint)` | `scope.rectFilled(x, y, w, h, color)` | Zero allocations |
| **Rectangle Outline**| `scope.rect(x, y, w, h, paint)` | `scope.rectStroke(x, y, w, h, color, width)` | Zero allocations |
| **Rounded Rectangle**| `scope.roundedRect(..., paint)`| `scope.roundedRectFilled(..., color)` | Zero allocations |
| **Circle / Ellipse** | `scope.circle(x, y, w, h, paint)`| `scope.circleFilled(x, y, w, h, color)` | Zero allocations |
| **Textured Quad** | `scope.texture(tex, placement, ...)` | `scope.addTexturedQuad(tex, x1, y1, ...)` | Zero allocations |

> [!TIP]
> In widget render methods, always prefer the `*Filled` and `*Stroke` overloads with constant or pre-allocated `ColorView` instances for maximum framerate stability.

draw.scope.section.vector.title: Vector Paths, Meshes & Ribbons
draw.scope.section.vector.body:
For custom procedural visuals, node graphs, map connections, and complex vector art, `DrawScope` offers rich path and polygon operations.

### Procedural Ribbons

The `ribbon(...)` method generates smooth, continuous textured ribbons along arbitrary polyline paths with automatic miter joints and butt caps:

- **Graph Connections**: Ideal for wiring, fluid pipes, and node-graph curves.
- **Texture Tiling**: When using textures with `REPEAT` wrap mode and specifying `textureLength` equal to the tile size, the texture repeats seamlessly along the ribbon length without elongation.

### Direct Vertex Polygons & Meshes

- **Polygons**: `addPolyline`, `addConvexPolyFilled`, and `addConcavePolyFilled` (using ear-clipping triangulation).
- **Meshes**: `addMesh(DrawMesh, TextureHandle)` allows precomputed indexed vertex meshes to be submitted in a single backend call.
- **Quads & Triangles**: `addQuadFilled`, `addTriangleFilled`, and `addRectFilledMultiColor` for smooth 4-corner color gradients.

texture.handle.title: TextureHandle
texture.handle.summary: Backend-neutral texture resource interface providing dimensions, sampling options, and native object access.
texture.handle.section.overview.title: Architecture & Backend Decoupling
texture.handle.section.overview.body:
`TextureHandle` is UniGUI's core abstraction representing a 2D image asset.

### Backend-Neutral Design

Widgets and custom renderers in UniGUI never interact directly with low-level graphics handles such as OpenGL texture IDs, DirectX descriptors, or platform-specific objects like Minecraft's `ResourceLocation`. Instead, all rendering commands (`DrawScope#texture`, `DrawScope#nineSlice`) record a reference to `TextureHandle`.

| Characteristic | UniGUI Approach | Direct Graphics API Approach |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Portability** | Runs unchanged across vanilla, Canvas, Iris/Oculus, or headless servers | Tied to specific OpenGL state or mod loaders |
| **Lifecycle** | Managed by UniGUI texture managers and asset providers | Manual `glGenTextures` and `glDeleteTextures` |
| **Sampling** | Immutable `TextureOptions` attached directly to the handle | Global sampler state changes in render loops |
| **Batching** | O(1) comparison via stable `id()` and packed options | Pointer or handle comparison with driver pipeline flushes |

!!! tip "Stable IDs for Pipeline Batching"
    UniGUI's render backends group consecutive textured quads into shared draw calls when they share the same `id()` and sampler state. Keep IDs consistent across frames to maximize draw-call batching efficiency.
texture.handle.section.dimensions.title: Dimensions & UV Mapping
texture.handle.section.options.title: Sampler Options & Caching
texture.handle.section.options.body:
Every `TextureHandle` exposes `options()`, returning an immutable `TextureOptions` instance.

- **Minification & Magnification Filtering**: `TextureFilter.NEAREST` for retro pixel-art or `TextureFilter.LINEAR` for smooth vector rasters.
- **UV Wrapping**: `TextureWrap.CLAMP_TO_EDGE` to eliminate border bleeding or `TextureWrap.REPEAT` for seamless wallpaper tiling.
- **Pre-computed State Key**: Options provide an integer key via `TextureOptions#packed()`, allowing backends to look up pre-created OpenGL sampler objects in O(1) time without allocating heap keys.
texture.handle.section.native.title: Native Handle Access
texture.handle.section.native.body:
`TextureHandle#nativeHandle()` returns the underlying graphics object used by the active platform:

- In Minecraft environments: Typically a `ResourceLocation` or `AbstractTexture`.
- In raw OpenGL / GLFW environments: Typically an `Integer` holding the OpenGL texture name.
- In mock / test environments: Returns `null` or a test identifier.

> [!WARNING]
> Custom widgets must avoid casting `nativeHandle()` directly. Rely exclusively on `DrawScope` methods to maintain cross-platform compatibility across client renderers and headless server environments.

paint.title: Paint
paint.summary: Styling descriptor for draw commands that configures color, stroke width, fill/stroke modes, Porter-Duff blending, and dashed lines.
paint.section.overview.title: Overview & Architecture
paint.section.overview.body:
`Paint` describes the visual attributes applied to vector shapes, geometric paths, textured surfaces, and drop shadows in UniGUI.

### Responsibilities

- **Coloring**: Encapsulates RGBA color view (`ColorView`) with fluent mutations.
- **Geometry Styling**: Toggles between solid interior fill (`stroke = false`) and outline perimeter stroke (`stroke = true`) with arbitrary pixel thickness.
- **Alpha Compositing**: Directs GPU hardware blending with `BlendMode` (NORMAL, ADDITIVE, MULTIPLY, SCREEN).
- **Line Patterns**: Configures dashed borders (`dash(length, gap)`) and animated pattern phases (`dashOffset`).
paint.section.copy.title: Deferred Copy Semantics
paint.section.copy.body:
`Paint` is deliberately designed as a **mutable object** to enable clean, fluent method chaining during widget preparation.

However, UniGUI's deferred draw-list architecture guarantees isolation:

> [!NOTE]
> When `DrawScope` creates a `DrawCommand`, it internally copies or snapshots the current `Paint` state. Any subsequent modifications made to your `Paint` instance will **never** alter or corrupt commands that were already recorded earlier in the frame.
paint.section.modes.title: Fill vs Stroke Modes
paint.section.blend.title: Blend Modes & Compositing
paint.section.blend.body:
Configure Porter-Duff hardware blending with `paint.blend(BlendMode)`:

| Blend Mode | Primary Use Cases | Visual Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `BlendMode.NORMAL` | Standard UI elements, opaque/translucent panels | Alpha-blended alpha-over compositing |
| `BlendMode.ADDITIVE` | Magic glows, particle sparks, neon selection lasers | Source color is added to destination, brightening pixels |
| `BlendMode.MULTIPLY` | Ambient occlusion drops, realistic soft shadows | Colors are multiplied, darkening underlying background |
| `BlendMode.SCREEN` | Soft light highlights, holograms | Inverted multiply creating smooth bright luminescence |
paint.section.dash.title: Dashed Borders & Animated Ants
paint.section.dash.body:
Stroked paths and shapes support dash patterns specified in UI pixels:

```java
Paint dashPaint = Paint.stroke(ColorView.rgb(0, 180, 255), 1.5f)
        .dash(6.0f, 4.0f) // 6px segment, 4px gap
        .dashOffset((System.currentTimeMillis() / 20.0f) % 10.0f); // animated marching ants
```

Calling `clearDash()` resets the paint back to a continuous solid line.

texture.options.title: TextureOptions
texture.options.summary: Immutable texture sampling configuration defining min/mag filtering, UV wrapping, mipmaps, and premultiplied alpha.
texture.options.section.overview.title: Overview & Immutable Design
texture.options.section.overview.body:
`TextureOptions` defines how GPU hardware samples a texture when rendering quads, meshes, and nine-slice panels.

### Immutable Semantics

`TextureOptions` does not own the underlying GPU resource; it only describes the desired sampler behavior. Every modifier method returns a new `TextureOptions` instance (or returns `this` if the requested value is already present), preventing accidental side-effects:

```java
TextureOptions base = TextureOptions.defaults();
TextureOptions linearWithRepeat = base.sampling(TextureFilter.LINEAR).wrap(TextureWrap.REPEAT);
```
texture.options.section.filtering.title: Filtering Modes (Nearest vs Linear)
texture.options.section.filtering.body:
`TextureFilter` determines pixel interpolation when scaling textures:

| Mode | Behavior | Best Used For |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `NEAREST` | Samples nearest discrete pixel without interpolation. | Pixel-art Minecraft textures, crisp item icons, UI borders. |
| `LINEAR` | Bilinear interpolation smoothly blending 4 adjacent texels. | High-res art, vector rasters, rotating elements, smooth scales. |
| `NEAREST_MIPMAP_NEAREST` | Nearest-neighbor filtering using nearest precomputed mipmap. | Heavily downscaled pixel-art surfaces. |
| `LINEAR_MIPMAP_LINEAR` | Trilinear filtering smoothly blending between mipmap levels. | 3D world projections, distant UI planes, elimination of moiré. |
texture.options.section.wrapping.title: UV Wrapping & Tiling (`TextureWrap`)
texture.options.section.wrapping.body:
Controls sampling when UV coordinates fall outside the standard `0.0..1.0` range:

- `CLAMP_TO_EDGE`: Clamps coordinates to the outermost border pixels. Default in UniGUI; prevents bleeding of opposite edges on textured panels.
- `REPEAT`: Tiles the texture infinitely. Ideal for animated scrolling backgrounds, striped caution tape, and procedural wallpapers.
- `MIRRORED_REPEAT`: Tiles the texture, mirroring orientation on alternating tiles. Ideal for symmetric organic patterns.
texture.options.section.alpha.title: Premultiplied Alpha & Mipmaps
texture.options.section.alpha.body:
### Premultiplied Alpha
When textures with transparent edges undergo bilinear filtering, standard straight alpha can produce dark halo artifacts because RGB channels bleed into zero-alpha black. Setting `premultipliedAlpha(true)` instructs the backend shader to blend using premultiplied alpha math (`src + dst * (1 - srcAlpha)`).

### Mipmaps
Enables automatic selection of pre-filtered lower-resolution texture copies during downscaling, eliminating crawling aliasing and shimmer artifacts.
texture.options.section.packed.title: 10-Bit Packed Key Architecture
texture.options.section.packed.body:
All sampling and wrapping parameters fit cleanly into a compact 10-bit integer key (`packed()`):

```text
Bits 0-1: MinFilter (NEAREST=0, LINEAR=1, NEAREST_MIP=2, LINEAR_MIP=3)
Bits 2-3: MagFilter (NEAREST=0, LINEAR=1)
Bits 4-5: WrapS (CLAMP=0, REPEAT=1, MIRRORED=2)
Bits 6-7: WrapT (CLAMP=0, REPEAT=1, MIRRORED=2)
Bit 8:    Mipmaps flag (0/1)
Bit 9:    Premultiplied Alpha flag (0/1)
```

Because `packed()` is a 10-bit integer, backends use a direct primitive array table (`SamplerState[1024]`) or fast switch statements, achieving O(1) cache lookups with **zero heap allocations**.

nine.slice.title: NineSlice
nine.slice.summary: Nine-patch scalable texture definition dividing an image into 4 unscaled corners, 4 single-axis edges, and 1 center area.
nine.slice.section.overview.title: Overview & 9-Patch Grid
nine.slice.section.overview.body:
`NineSlice` is UniGUI's model for scalable rectangular GUI elements (window chrome, button backgrounds, dialogue plates, and tooltips).

### The 9-Slice Slicing Grid

An image is divided into nine rectangular regions based on four border inset measurements:

```text
+------------+--------------------+------------+
| Top-Left   | Top Edge           | Top-Right  |
| (fixed)    | (stretched horiz)  | (fixed)    |
+------------+--------------------+------------+
| Left Edge  | Center             | Right Edge |
| (stretch V)| (stretched both)   | (stretch V)|
+------------+--------------------+------------+
| Bottom-Left| Bottom Edge        | Bottom-Right|
| (fixed)    | (stretched horiz)  | (fixed)    |
+------------+--------------------+------------+
```

Because the 4 corners remain at their 1:1 pixel scale, visual corners never blur or distort regardless of the target widget dimensions.

nine.slice.section.fill_center.title: Solid Panels vs Hollow Outlines
nine.slice.section.fill_center.body:
`DrawScope#nineSlice` accepts a boolean flag `fillCenter`:

- `fillCenter = true`: Renders all 9 quads (corners, edges, and center). Standard for solid dialogues and inventory panels.
- `fillCenter = false`: Omits the central quad (renders only the 8 border quads). Ideal for hollow selection rectangles, slot highlights, and transparent focus rings.

texture.group.title: TextureGroup
texture.group.summary: Ordered composite collection of TextureLayer instances rendered sequentially within shared base bounds.
texture.group.section.overview.title: Overview & Layer Compositing
texture.group.section.overview.body:
`TextureGroup` combines multiple `TextureLayer` descriptors into a single reusable visual asset.

### Multi-Layer Surface Architecture

Instead of managing multiple parallel texture fields inside a widget, `TextureGroup` bundles all layers together:
- Each layer manages its own `TextureHandle`, source UV rect, tint color, `ImageFit`, and nine-slice borders.
- Layers render in strict sequential order from index 0 to N-1 (background plates, frames, patterns, highlight overlays).
- Null textures in a layer are cleanly skipped without breaking the draw pipeline.
texture.group.section.builder.title: Fluent Builder Construction
texture.group.section.builder.body:
Construct a `TextureGroup` using static factories or the fluent `TextureGroup#builder()`:

```java
TextureGroup group = TextureGroup.builder()
        .add(backgroundTexture) // default layer settings
        .add(new TextureLayer(frameTexture).tint(ColorView.rgb(200, 200, 200)))
        .build();
```

shader.handle.title: ShaderHandle
shader.handle.summary: Identifier and container for UI shaders, referencing external resource paths or embedding GLSL source code.
shader.handle.section.overview.title: Architecture & GLSL Resolution
shader.handle.section.overview.body:
`ShaderHandle` represents a GPU shader pipeline used by `DrawCommandType.SHADER` and `DrawScope#shader`.

### Two Operating Modes

1. **Resource Identifier (`ShaderHandle.resource(id)`)**: Refers to a named shader resource (e.g. `minecraft:rendertype_gui` or a mod shader). The active `RenderBackend` queries registered `ShaderProvider` instances to resolve vertex and fragment source.
2. **Embedded GLSL Source (`ShaderHandle.source(...)` or `fragmentSource(...)`)**: Embeds vertex and/or fragment GLSL source strings directly in the handle for rapid procedural effects without packaging loose resource files.
shader.handle.section.execution.title: Shader Execution Pipeline
shader.handle.section.execution.body:
When drawing via `DrawScope#shader`:

1. `ShaderHandle` identifies the program.
2. `ShaderUniforms` supplies custom uniforms (resolution, time, colors, vectors).
3. `ShaderDrawOptions` configures blending and automatic built-in uniforms (`SquareVertex`).

Backends compile and cache GLSL programs keyed by `id()`. Redundant recompilation is avoided across frames.

shader.draw.options.summary: Backend-facing configuration for shader draw commands governing blending, built-in uniforms, and vertex offsets.
shader.draw.options.section.overview.bod:
`ShaderDrawOptions` configures GPU render state when executing custom shaders via `DrawScope#shader`.

- **Built-in Uniforms**: Automatically provides resolution, model-view projection matrices, and default inputs when `builtinUniforms = true`.
- **Blending**: Directs the backend whether to enable alpha blending during the shader pass.
- **Vertex Offset**: Adjusts coordinate alignment for fullscreen and sub-rect quad shaders.
shader.draw.options.section.builtins.bod:
When `builtinUniforms()` is enabled, the active backend automatically injects default shader parameters into the execution context:

- `SquareVertex`: Normalized vertex offset (default `-0.25f` preserving legacy quad shader compatibility).
- Standard projection and model-view matrices supplied by the underlying engine.

shader.uniforms.title: ShaderUniforms
shader.uniforms.summary: Mutable collection of named shader parameters (floats, ints, vectors, colors) passed to GPU programs.
shader.uniforms.section.overview.title: Overview & Insertion Order
shader.uniforms.section.overview.body:
`ShaderUniforms` holds named uniform values supplied to a shader draw command.

- **Insertion Order Preserved**: Backends iterate uniforms in stable insertion order, simplifying diagnostics and batching.
- **Defensive Copying**: Values are copied upon insertion, so callers can reuse temporary uniform or color objects.
- **Fluent Convenience API**: Direct setters for `float`, `int`, `vec2`, `vec3`, `vec4`, `ColorView`, and ARGB integers.

ribbon.mesh.title: RibbonMesh
ribbon.mesh.summary: Procedural textured ribbon mesh generator along polylines for rendering roads, cables, traces, pipelines, and graph edges.
ribbon.mesh.section.overview.title: Overview
ribbon.mesh.section.overview.body: `RibbonMesh` expands a 2D polyline (list of center points) into a triangulated strip with defined physical width. Each point produces a vertex pair left and right of the centerline. Adjacent pairs form two triangles with butt cap endpoints and clamped miter joins.
ribbon.mesh.section.geometry.title: Geometry & Miter Joins
ribbon.mesh.section.geometry.body: Internal joints calculate an averaged normal between neighboring segments (miter). To prevent sharp bends or 180° turnarounds from producing infinitely projecting spikes, the miter length is clamped by `miterLimit` (default 4.0 half-widths).
ribbon.mesh.section.uv.title: UV Mapping & Orientation
ribbon.mesh.section.uv.body: Coordinates are mapped such that `u` spans across the ribbon width (`0..1`) and `v` advances along the path as `distance / textureLength`. When texture wrapping is set to `REPEAT`, the texture tiles seamlessly without stretching. For vertical stripe textures (like cable or wire patterns), `swapUv(true)` rotates the texture 90° so `u` runs along the path and `v` across width.
ribbon.mesh.section.joints.title: Joint Dots & Corners
ribbon.mesh.section.joints.body: At very sharp corners where miter joins degenerate, enabling `jointDots(true)` places circular vertex disks (radii matching half the ribbon width) over joints, completely eliminating visual seams and gaps.
ribbon.mesh.section.culling.title: Culling & Clipping
ribbon.mesh.section.culling.body: The ribbon builder supports view rect clipping (`clip(x, y, w, h)`). Segments outside the viewport (expanded by the miter margin) are skipped without breaking the accumulated distance parameter `v`, ensuring textures stay aligned during scrolling.
ribbon.mesh.section.builder.title: Builder API
ribbon.mesh.section.builder.body: Construct ribbons via the fluent `RibbonMesh.builder(points)` for detailed customization (width, texture length, miter limit, closed loops, clipping, UV flipping), or use the one-shot convenience overload `RibbonMesh.ribbon(...)` for standard strips.
ribbon.mesh.example.cable.title: Building a Textured Power Cable
ribbon.mesh.example.track.title: Closed Circuit Loop with Joint Disks
ribbon.mesh.example.track.code:
List<DrawPoint> corners = List.of(
    new DrawPoint(50.0f, 50.0f),
    new DrawPoint(250.0f, 50.0f),
    new DrawPoint(200.0f, 180.0f),
    new DrawPoint(80.0f, 150.0f)
);
DrawMesh track = RibbonMesh.builder(corners)
    .width(16.0f)
    .textureLength(48.0f)
    .closed(true)
    .jointDots(true)
    .jointSegments(16)
    .build(ColorView.rgb(200, 200, 200));
scope.addMesh(track, roadTexture);

ribbon.options.title: RibbonOptions
ribbon.options.summary: Immutable value object configuring polyline ribbon mesh generation, corner miters, joint dots, and UV texture transforms.
ribbon.options.section.overview.title: Overview
ribbon.options.section.overview.body: `RibbonOptions` groups ribbon generation parameters (closed loop, miter limit, UV swapping, axis flipping, and circular joint dots) into an immutable structure. It eliminates multi-parameter overload explosions across DrawScope and RenderContext.
ribbon.options.section.immutability.body: Every modifier method returns a new `RibbonOptions` instance or returns the current instance if the requested value is unchanged. The shared baseline instance is retrieved via `RibbonOptions.defaults()`.
ribbon.options.section.caching.title: Packed Bitfield & Caching
ribbon.options.section.caching.body: All configuration flags, quantized miter limit, and joint segment counts are packed into a single 32-bit integer via `packed()`. This allows zero-allocation cache lookups when caching precomputed ribbon meshes in widgets.

draw.list.title: DrawList
draw.list.summary: Retained frame command buffer recording backend-neutral draw primitives, managing command recycling pools, and providing multi-channel layering.
draw.list.section.overview.title: Overview
draw.list.section.overview.body: Widgets do not draw directly to the GPU. Instead, drawing operations emit `DrawCommand` instances into a `DrawList`. At the end of the frame, the active `RenderBackend` iterates over the list to perform state sorting, geometry batching, texture binding, and GPU draws.
draw.list.section.pooling.title: Command Lifecycle & Pooling
draw.list.section.pooling.body: To prevent garbage collection overhead during high-frequency UI rendering, `DrawList` maintains a pool of recycled `DrawCommand` objects (up to 8,192 instances). Internal helpers obtain pooled commands via `obtain(DrawCommandType)` and return them during `clear()`.
draw.list.section.channels.title: Multi-Channel Layering
draw.list.section.channels.body: Channels allow widgets to emit draw commands into separate virtual layers (e.g. background, content, overlay, tooltip) during a single traversal without reordering code. Calling `channelsSplit(n)` divides recording into channels, `channelsSetCurrent(i)` switches the active target, and `channelsMerge()` flattens all layers into consecutive commands.
draw.list.section.paths.title: Vector Paths
draw.list.section.paths.body: `DrawList` owns a dedicated `VectorPath` builder accessible via `path()`. Procedural shapes, curves, and contours can be constructed incrementally into this shared path without allocating temporary geometry objects.
draw.list.section.backend.title: Backend Consumption
draw.list.section.backend.body: Backends can access commands either through an unmodifiable `List<DrawCommand>` via `commands()` or via direct array access through `commandElements()` and `size()` for maximum iteration performance.
draw.list.example.channels.title: Layering Background and Foreground with Channels
draw.list.example.backend.title: Iterating Recorded Commands in a Backend Loop

ui.render.policy.title: UiRenderPolicy
ui.render.policy.summary: Frame-rate and invalidation policy controlling how frequently retained UI trees are rebuilt and rendered.
ui.render.policy.section.overview.title: Overview
ui.render.policy.section.overview.body: `UiRenderPolicy` dictates whether the runtime redraws the UI on every game tick, only when widget state changes (dirty signal), at a capped FPS, or locked to display VSYNC. This prevents unnecessary GPU and CPU overhead for static interfaces.
ui.render.policy.section.modes.title: Render Modes
ui.render.policy.section.modes.body:
- `CONTINUOUS`: Rebuilds and renders every frame. Ideal for fluid 60+ FPS animations, procedural shaders, and editor viewports.
- `ON_DIRTY`: Renders only when an explicit invalidation/dirty signal is raised. Conserves significant GPU/CPU cycles for static menus and HUDs.
- `FIXED_FPS`: Clamps rendering frequency to a specified target frame rate (e.g. 30 FPS).
- `VSYNC`: Synchronizes rendering intervals with the window display refresh rate.
ui.render.policy.section.power.title: Performance and Power Efficiency
ui.render.policy.section.power.body: Static screens with complex layout trees can cause substantial overhead if re-rendered every tick. Switching to `onDirty()` reduces draw-call generation to zero during idle states, re-rendering only when user input or data events arrive.

rich.text.title: RichText
rich.text.summary: Immutable multi-style rich text model supporting styled runs, fonts, brushes, gradients, and inline content spans.
rich.text.section.overview.title: Overview
rich.text.section.overview.body: `RichText` represents formatted text composed of multiple style runs and optional inline content atoms (such as icons or custom graphics). It exposes a dual projection: `spans()` for complete layout atoms (including inline spans) and `runs()` for legacy text-only consumers.
rich.text.section.spans.title: Spans and Projections
rich.text.section.spans.body: Text is stored as an immutable list of `RichTextSpan` instances. Text runs (`TextRun`) contain character sequences with dedicated font faces, pixel sizes, colors, tracking, and transforms. Inline content spans (`InlineContentSpan`) describe atomic layout boxes (with fallback text) rendered by procedural callbacks.
rich.text.section.inline.title: Inline Content and Icons
rich.text.section.inline.body: Inline atoms flow seamlessly within the text stream. They participate in line wrapping, measurement, and alignment without creating separate widget hierarchy nodes. Icons and custom renderers inherit parent scissor clipping and transforms automatically.
rich.text.section.brushes.title: Text Brushes and Gradients
rich.text.section.brushes.body: RichText supports procedural brush fills via `TextBrush`. The `withBrush()` and `withLinearGradient()` methods apply solid colors or multi-color gradients across all text runs while preserving existing color tints.
rich.text.section.transform.title: Text Transforms and Slicing
rich.text.section.transform.body: Use `slice(start, end)` to extract substring ranges using plain-text character offsets. Whole inline spans within the range are preserved, while partial overlaps degrade safely to fallback plain text. `withTextStyle()` allows batch customization of font sizes, letter spacing (tracking), and case transformations.
rich.text.section.builder.title: Builder API
rich.text.section.builder.body: Construct mixed text and icon flows fluently using `RichText.builder()`. Set style attributes (`font`, `size`, `color`, `brush`, `tracking`, `transform`) that apply to subsequent `append()` calls, or insert inline graphics via `icon()` and `inline()`.
rich.text.example.mixed.title: Building Rich Text with Text and Inline Icons
rich.text.example.mixed.code:
RichText text = RichText.builder()
    .append("Status: ")
    .icon("icon:ok", checkTexture, 12.0f)
    .color(ColorView.rgb(80, 220, 100))
    .append(" All systems online")
    .build();

    45.0f

text.overflow.mode.title: TextOverflowMode
text.overflow.mode.summary: Enumeration configuring visual clipping, truncation, shrinking, or marquee scrolling when text exceeds available bounds.
text.overflow.mode.section.overview.body: `TextOverflowMode` governs how UI widgets handle text content that does not fit into allocated layout dimensions. It controls visual presentation without altering underlying text layout metrics or plain text strings.
text.overflow.mode.section.modes.title: Overflow Behaviors
text.overflow.mode.section.modes.body:
- `VISIBLE`: Text renders fully and may spill past widget boundaries.
- `CLIP`: Scissor clips text strictly to the widget bounds.
- `ELLIPSIS`: Truncates overflowing single-line text and appends an ellipsis (`...`), guaranteeing the result fits.
- `SHRINK_TO_FIT`: Dynamically scales font size down until the entire line fits the available width.
- `MARQUEE_ON_HOVER`: Clipped when idle; smoothly scrolls back and forth when hovered by the cursor.

label.overflow(TextOverflowMode.ELLIPSIS);

text.engine.title: TextEngine
text.engine.summary: Core text layout, line-wrapping, dimension measurement, and inline-content rendering engine.
text.engine.section.overview.title: Overview
text.engine.section.overview.body: `TextEngine` is the centralized subsystem responsible for measuring character widths, wrapping long text runs across multiple lines, aligning blocks horizontally/vertically, and laying out embedded inline spans (icons, textures, badges) alongside regular text.
text.engine.section.measurement.title: Text and Content Measurement
text.engine.section.measurement.body: Measurement methods compute line dimensions (`measureLineWidth`) and block heights (`measureTextHeight`) taking into account font ascent, descent, character code-points, and atomic inline spans. The `minContentWidth` method determines the minimum width required to display the longest word without clipping.
text.engine.section.wrapping.title: Line Wrapping
text.engine.section.wrapping.body: `wrapLines()` splits rich text across word boundaries to fit within a given maximum width (`maxWidth`). If single words exceed the available line width, they are broken at character boundaries to prevent line overflows.
text.engine.section.rendering.title: Rendering and Inline Content
text.engine.section.rendering.body: When rendering plain text runs, TextEngine delegates directly to `RenderBackend`. If inline spans exist, TextEngine computes exact coordinates for each atom and invokes its `InlineContentRenderer` with final screen bounds.

default.font.registry.title: DefaultFontRegistry
default.font.registry.summary: Standard font registry loading TrueType and Type1 fonts from streams, files, or platform system fonts without Minecraft dependencies.
default.font.registry.section.overview.b: `DefaultFontRegistry` provides the default standalone font management implementation. It allows registering fonts from filesystem paths, resource input streams, or byte arrays, and supports system font fallbacks without depending on Minecraft client asset loaders.
default.font.registry.section.registrati: Fonts are registered under unique identifier strings via `register()`. Both TrueType (`.ttf`) and Type1 font formats are automatically parsed and mapped into `FontFace` objects.
default.font.registry.section.system.bod: The registry maintains a default font face accessible via `defaultFace()`. If no custom font has been set, it automatically loads a system fallback (e.g. `SansSerif`). Custom system families can be registered via `registerSystem()`.
Implements `AutoCloseable`. Calling `close()` clears all registered font faces and resets the default font reference, preventing memory leaks during application reload.

uni.screen.title: UniScreen
uni.screen.summary: Minecraft-independent description of a standalone screen/GUI window in UniGUI.
uni.screen.section.overview.title: Overview
uni.screen.section.overview.body: `UniScreen` is the primary descriptor for standalone GUI screens in UniGUI. It wraps a root `Widget` tree, provides window title configuration, custom UI scaling (`uiScale`), game GUI scaling synchronization, render invalidation policies (`UiRenderPolicy`), default font assignment, and keyboard input interception before passing events to focused widgets.
uni.screen.section.lifecycle.title: Lifecycle and Opening
uni.screen.section.lifecycle.body: Opening and closing screens is completely backend-independent. Invoking `openGui()` requests the active `RenderBackend` to open the screen (e.g. creating and setting a Minecraft `Screen` wrapper or standalone window). The `onClose` callback triggers when the screen is dismissed.
uni.screen.section.scaling.title: Scaling and Input Interception
uni.screen.section.scaling.body:
Screens can inherit Minecraft's GUI scale (`scaleWithGameGui(true)`) or enforce a fixed scaling factor via `uiScale(float)`.

The `KeyboardInputHandler` allows global shortcut handling (e.g. Esc, search hotkeys) before focused widgets receive the event.

uni.render.layer.summary: Minecraft-independent configuration for an overlay or HUD UI layer.
uni.render.layer.section.overview.title: Overview
uni.render.layer.section.overview.body: `UniRenderLayer` represents an isolated layer rendered either in the in-game HUD or over an active GUI screen. It binds a root `Widget`, an optional `UIContext`, custom post-processing shader chains (`UiPostEffectChain`), render policies, and lifecycle hooks.
uni.render.layer.section.post_effects.bo: Layers support post-processing filters via `postEffect(...)`, applying Gaussian blur, CRT scanlines, bloom, or color grading directly to the rendered layer buffer before blitting to the framebuffer.
uni.render.layer.section.cache.title: Cache Invalidation and Lifecycle
uni.render.layer.section.cache.body: Layers implementing `AutoCloseable` can be removed from rendering via `close()`. When rendered with dirty-tracking, `invalidateRenderCache()` signals the runtime to redraw the layer content.

uni.hud.render.section.overview.title: Overview
uni.hud.render.section.overview.body: `UniHudRender` provides static helper methods to bind widget trees or `UniRenderLayer` instances to the game's in-game HUD (`UniRenderTarget.HUD`). Layers can define dynamic visibility predicates and z-ordering priority.

- **Default Priority**: 0

uni.screen.overlay.render.summary: Minecraft-independent entry point for overlays rendered on top of active GUI screens.
uni.screen.overlay.render.section.overvi: `UniScreenOverlayRender` registers layers targeting `UniRenderTarget.SCREEN_OVERLAY`. These layers render on top of any open screen (vanilla inventories, mod containers, custom screens) without replacing the underlying screen hierarchy.
uni.screen.overlay.render.section.use_ca:
Screen overlays are suited for features that remain persistent across menu transitions:

- **Recipe and item browsers** (JEI/REI/EMI style sidebars).
- **In-game notifications and toasts** displayed above open menus.
- **Debug inspectors** and UI hierarchy visualizers.
- **Pinned tooltips** or assistance windows.

uni.render.target.title: UniRenderTarget
uni.render.target.summary: Host rendering hook target for a neutral UniGUI render layer.
uni.render.target.section.overview.title: Overview
uni.render.target.section.overview.body:
`UniRenderTarget` defines the target rendering stage where a `UniRenderLayer` is hooked by the underlying platform runtime:

- `HUD`: Rendered during the in-game HUD rendering phase (crosshair, status bars, hotbar).
- `SCREEN_OVERLAY`: Rendered over open GUI screens and menus.

uni.render.layer.registration.summary: Backend-neutral handle for a registered render layer.
uni.render.layer.registration.section.ov: `UniRenderLayerRegistration` encapsulates a registered layer in the active backend. It allows dynamically enabling or disabling the layer, changing its z-priority, updating its visibility predicate, and cleanly unregistering it via `close()`.
uni.render.layer.registration.section.li: Since `UniRenderLayerRegistration` implements `AutoCloseable`, it can be managed with try-with-resources or closed when a feature is toggled off, instantly unhooking both the backend registration and the layer itself.

ui.post.effects.title: UiPostEffects
ui.post.effects.summary: Built-in catalog of standard post-processing effects and embedded shader sources.
ui.post.effects.section.overview.title: Overview
ui.post.effects.section.overview.body:
`UiPostEffects` provides ready-to-use post-processing effect definitions and embedded GLSL shaders for HUD layers, overlays, and modal screens.

### Built-in Effect Presets

- `unigui:passthrough`: Identity copy pass without visual modification.
- `unigui:tint`: Color overlay tint with customizable color and intensity amount.
- `unigui:vignette`: Radial border darkening with configurable radius, softness, and color.
- `unigui:barrel_distortion`: Curved lens warping for helmet, visor, or CRT monitor simulation.
- `unigui:chromatic_aberration`: RGB color channel separation along directional vectors.
- `unigui:scanline`: Animated horizontal scanlines simulating retro displays.
ui.post.effects.section.usage.title: Registering and Applying Built-in Effects
ui.post.effects.section.usage.body: Call `UiPostEffects.ensureRegistered()` to register standard definitions and the built-in shader provider into global registries. Applying an effect to a layer is as simple as calling `layer.postEffect("unigui:vignette")`.

ui.post.effect.chain.section.overview.bo:
`UiPostEffectChain` encapsulates a sequence of post-processing shader passes applied to an offscreen layer buffer. A chain can be empty (`none()`), reference a registered effect ID (`of("unigui:tint")`), or hold inline pass instances.

Backend renderers resolve chains lazily during render time. If a referenced effect ID is unregistered or post-processing is unsupported, rendering seamlessly falls back to normal direct drawing without crashing.

ui.post.effect.blend.mode.title: UiPostEffectBlendMode
ui.post.effect.blend.mode.summary: Blending behavior for a post-processing shader pass.
ui.post.effect.blend.mode.section.overvi:
`UiPostEffectBlendMode` instructs the rendering backend how to blend the output of a shader pass into the target framebuffer:

- `REPLACE`: Overwrites target pixels directly without alpha blending. Standard for intermediate ping-pong buffer passes.
- `ALPHA_BLEND`: Standard transparency blending (`SRC_ALPHA, ONE_MINUS_SRC_ALPHA`).
- `ADDITIVE`: Additive blending for glow, laser, and light bloom overlays.

boolean blend = mode.blendEnabled();

debug.overlay.settings.summary: Configuration for placement, scaling, and sampling of the built-in performance overlay.
`DebugOverlaySettings` is the mutable configuration returned by `UIContext#debugOverlaySettings`. It controls where the built-in performance overlay appears, its UI scale, the number of retained chart samples, and its distance from the viewport edge. Setters normalize unsafe values, so configuration can be updated directly from editor controls or hotkeys.
debug.overlay.settings.section.hotkeys.b:
Minecraft screens and render layers provide the following built-in shortcuts:

| Shortcut | Action |
| --- | --- |
| `Ctrl+Shift+P` | Toggles the profiler overlay. |
| `Ctrl+Shift++`, `Ctrl+Shift+=`, or numpad `+` | Increases overlay scale by `0.25`. |
| `Ctrl+Shift+-` or numpad `-` | Decreases overlay scale by `0.25`. |

The main-row plus key is reported as `=` by GLFW, so both plus/equal notation refers to the same binding. A shortcut runs once per physical key press; key-repeat callbacks are consumed without applying the action again. These bindings require the standard `DefaultUIContext`. Scale changes remain clamped by `DebugOverlaySettings` to the inclusive range `0.25` through `4.0`.

style.section.overview.body: A `Style` stores values by typed `StyleKey` and `WidgetState`. Querying a state may fall back to `NORMAL`, then to the fallback supplied by the caller. Use `MutableStyle` to build values in Java, `Style#fromText` for inline declarations, or `Style#from` for one XML `<Style>` element.

style.section.cascade.body: `Style` is one layer, not the whole theme cascade. `StylePack` combines theme tokens, fallback values, widget bindings, and matching definitions. A local widget style is applied after theme layers. Use `StylePack#from` when XML contains selectors, named definitions, event animations, or renderer bindings.
