widget.title: Widget
widget.summary: Base contract for any UI tree element: lifecycle, layout, rendering, input, and styling.
widget.section.overview.title: Overview
widget.section.overview.body:
`Widget` is the root interface for every element in the UniGUI tree hierarchy. It unifies layout measurement, positioning, visual styling, hit testing, event dispatching, frame tick updates, and procedural drawing into a single coherent contract.

It extends `EventEmitter`, allowing every widget in the tree to subscribe to and emit strongly typed events.

| Subsystem | Core Contract | Role & Execution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Hierarchy** | `parent()`, `children()`, `uiContext()` | Defines parent-child tree relations, coordinate spaces, and window context. |
| **Layout** | `measure()`, `arrange()`, `desiredSize()`, `layoutBounds()` | Two-pass layout: computes size request then commits final geometry bounds. |
| **Visual Styling** | `style()`, `styleId()`, `styleClasses()` | Inline CSS declarations, class tokens, and Theme / StylePack rules. |
| **Input & Focus** | `handle()`, `mouseCursorAt()`, `focusable()`, `focusScope()` | Dispatches mouse, pointer, and keyboard events; manages focus scopes. |
| **Invalidation** | `invalidate()`, `clearInvalidation()`, `invalidationFlags()` | Tracks dirty layout and visual bits, avoiding unnecessary reflows. |
| **Render & Tick** | `render()`, `tick()`, `dispose()` | Per-frame state updates, procedural rendering into draw list, and resource disposal. |

!!! tip "Extending WidgetBase vs Implementing Widget"
    In almost all cases, custom controls should extend `WidgetBase` rather than implementing `Widget` from scratch.     `WidgetBase` provides complete implementations for retained render caching, FLIP animations, style resolution, and invalidation bubbling.
widget.section.lifecycle.title: Lifecycle & Pipeline
widget.section.lifecycle.body:
Each frame, the UniGUI runtime executes a structured pipeline across the widget hierarchy:

1. **`measure(LayoutContext)`**: Calculates requested dimensions (`desiredSize()`) based on content and layout constraints.
2. **`arrange(RectView)`**: Commits final positioned bounds and aligns child widgets.
3. **`handle(Event)`**: Processes routed input, mouse, and keyboard events.
4. **`tick(FrameContext)`**: Updates transitions, spring animations, and time-based state.
5. **`render(RenderContext)`**: Emits drawing commands into the active draw list.
6. **`dispose()`**: Cleans up internal widget resources prior to removal from the tree.
widget.section.tree.title: Tree Hierarchy & Structure
widget.section.tree.body:
Widgets form a directed tree structure managed by `parent()` and `children()`:

- **`parent()`**: Returns the owning container widget, or `null` if the widget is the root or unattached.
- **`children()`**: Returns child widgets in traversal order.
- **Order semantics**: Children order defines rendering order (back-to-front: first child drawn first, last child on top) and hit-testing order (front-to-back: topmost child receives pointer events first).
- **`uiContext()`**: Provides access to the root window, dispatcher, font registry, and input services.
widget.section.style.title: Style & Layout
widget.section.style.body:
UniGUI strictly decouples geometry from visual presentation:

- **Geometry**: Governed by `layoutBounds()` and `desiredSize()`, configured through `LayoutStyle`.
- **Visual Style**: Assigned via `styleId(...)` (referencing a StylePack rule), `styleClasses(...)` (CSS classes), or inline declarations via `style("background: #333; radius: 8;")`.
- **Style Scope**: Widgets can declare `styleScope(true)` to isolate local style overrides from propagating to outer trees.
widget.section.focus.title: Input, Focus & Interaction
widget.section.focus.body:
Interactive state is controlled through dedicated status flags:

| State Flag | Purpose & Effect |
| --- | --- |
| **`visibility()`** | `VISIBLE` participates in layout and rendering; `HIDDEN` preserves layout space but hides visual; `COLLAPSED` leaves layout entirely. |
| **`enabled()`** | Controls user interactivity. Disabled widgets ignore events and receive the `:disabled` style pseudo-class. |
| **`hovered()`** | Indicates whether the mouse cursor is currently over this widget. |
| **`mouseCursorAt()`** | Returns the cursor shape (e.g. `HAND`, `TEXT`) when hovered at local coordinates. |
| **`focusable()`** | Determines whether the widget can accept keyboard focus via Tab navigation or clicking. |
| **`focusScope()`** | Traps Tab-cycling inside this subtree (crucial for modal dialogs and popup panels). |
| **`focusOrder()`** | Explicit relative priority index for Tab ordering. |
widget.section.invalidation.title: Dirty State & Invalidation
widget.section.invalidation.body:
To achieve maximum frame rates, UniGUI skips layout passes and retained draw command generation for clean subtrees:

- **`invalidate(flags)`**: Marks dirty bits from `InvalidationFlags` (`LAYOUT`, `VISUAL`, `RETAINED_RENDER`). Layout flags bubble upward to root.
- **`clearInvalidation(flags)`**: Clears processed dirty flags after the pipeline pass completes.
- **`subtreeInvalidationFlags()`**: Returns combined bitmask of pending dirty flags for the widget and all descendants.
widget.example.events.title: Subscribing to widget events
widget.example.skeleton.title: Creating a custom widget
event.emitter.title: EventEmitter
event.emitter.summary: Contract for objects that can subscribe to and dispatch typed events.
event.emitter.section.overview.title: Overview
event.emitter.section.overview.body:
`EventEmitter` is the foundational event subscription and dispatch contract implemented by `Widget` and other observable UniGUI components. It provides a strongly typed, zero-reflection interface for registering event listeners and emitting events synchronously.

Every event is keyed by an `EventType<T>`, eliminating string keys or reflection overhead.
event.emitter.section.subscription.title: Subscription Lifecycle
event.emitter.section.subscription.body:
Calling `on(EventType, listener)` registers a listener and returns an `EventSubscription` handle:

- **Unregistering**: Call `subscription.unsubscribe()` or `subscription.close()` to stop receiving events.
- **Scoped Cleanup**: Because `EventSubscription` implements `AutoCloseable`, it works seamlessly with `try-with-resources` or `EventScope` for automated unregistration during screen or widget teardown.
- **Thread Safety**: Implementations ensure that listener registration and unregistration during active dispatch passes do not throw concurrent modification errors.
event.emitter.section.cancelled.title: Event Cancellation
event.emitter.section.cancelled.body:
Events in UniGUI implement cooperative cancellation via `Event.cancel()` and `Event.isCancelled()`.

- **Standard Listener**: `on(type, listener)` automatically ignores events that have already been cancelled.
- **Audit / Monitor Listener**: Use `on(type, true, listener)` with `receiveCancelled = true` to receive events even after upstream handlers have called `cancel()`. Useful for diagnostics, telemetry, or catch-all handlers.
event.emitter.example.subscribe.title: Listening for events
event.emitter.example.emit.title: Dispatching events
event.emitter.example.emit.code:
// Synchronously dispatches event to all matching listeners
widget.emit(new ButtonClickEvent(widget));
event.emitter.method.on.title: Subscribe to event
event.emitter.method.on.summary: Registers a listener for the specified event type.
event.emitter.method.on_cancelled.title: Subscribe including cancelled events
event.emitter.method.on_cancelled.summar: Registers a listener with control over receiving cancelled events.
event.emitter.method.emit.title: Emit event
event.emitter.method.emit.summary: Dispatches an event synchronously to all registered listeners.
fast.event.bus.title: FastEventBus
fast.event.bus.summary: Ultra-fast, lock-free, zero-allocation event bus without reflection or hash-maps.
fast.event.bus.section.overview.title: Overview
fast.event.bus.section.overview.body: `FastEventBus` is the high-performance event bus engine powering UniGUI. Designed specifically for performance-critical scenarios such as game rendering loops and input dispatching, it eliminates runtime reflection, hash map lookups, and allocation garbage during dispatch.
fast.event.bus.section.architecture.body:
Traditional event buses use class-to-method reflection maps or string identifiers, which generate iterator allocations, boxing overhead, and hash lookups on every dispatch.

`FastEventBus` solves this through dense integer indexing:

- **`EventType<T>`**: Each event type receives an automatically assigned sequential integer index (`id = 0, 1, 2...`).
- **AtomicReferenceArray**: Listeners are stored in contiguous typed arrays indexed directly by event ID.
- **Direct Iteration**: `fire()` directly indexes into the array and loops through listeners with zero intermediate objects.
fast.event.bus.section.concurrency.title: Concurrency & Thread Safety
fast.event.bus.section.concurrency.body:
The bus uses lock-free reads combined with copy-on-write writes:

- **`fire()`**: Entirely lock-free. Reads the current listener array atomically and iterates over it.
- **`subscribe()` / `unsubscribe()`**: Synchronized and use Copy-On-Write array duplication, keeping reader threads completely unblocked.
- **Exception Isolation**: Exceptions thrown inside a listener callback are caught and logged via SLF4J, ensuring one broken handler never halts dispatch to other listeners.
fast.event.bus.example.basic.title: Subscribe and fire
fast.event.bus.example.typed.title: Custom record event
fast.event.bus.method.subscribe.title: Subscribe listener
fast.event.bus.method.subscribe.summary: Registers a listener for an event type using copy-on-write.
fast.event.bus.method.unsubscribe.title: Unsubscribe listener
fast.event.bus.method.unsubscribe.summar: Removes a listener using copy-on-write array shrinking.
fast.event.bus.method.fire.title: Fire event
fast.event.bus.method.fire.summary: Dispatches an event lock-free with zero garbage allocation.
event.scope.title: EventScope
event.scope.summary: Scoped lifecycle manager for event subscriptions.
event.scope.section.overview.title: Overview
event.scope.section.overview.body:
`EventScope` is an `AutoCloseable` container that tracks event subscriptions created during a component's lifecycle. In interactive UIs, forgetting to unregister event listeners when navigating away from a screen or destroying a dialog is one of the most common causes of memory leaks and ghost updates.

By binding listener subscriptions to an `EventScope`, all registered listeners can be cleaned up in a single call.
event.scope.section.lifecycle.title: Lifecycle Management
event.scope.section.lifecycle.body:
- **`listen(event, listener)`**: Subscribes to the event and tracks the returned subscription.
- **`clear()`**: Unsubscribes all currently tracked listeners in reverse order, while leaving the scope open for future registrations.
- **`close()`**: Marks the scope as permanently closed and unsubscribes all listeners. Subsequent calls to `listen()` return `EventSubscription.NOOP`.
- **`EventScope.noop()`**: Factory creating a permanently disabled scope that ignores registrations, useful for optional subscription patterns.
event.scope.example.screen.title: Screen lifecycle integration
event.scope.method.noop.title: No-op scope
event.scope.method.noop.summary: Returns a disabled scope that ignores all registrations.
event.scope.method.listen.title: Tracked listen
event.scope.method.listen.summary: Subscribes a listener to the event and tracks it for cleanup.
event.scope.method.clear.title: Clear subscriptions
event.scope.method.clear.summary: Unsubscribes all currently tracked listeners without closing the scope.
event.scope.method.close.title: Close scope
event.scope.method.close.summary: Closes the scope and unregisters all tracked listeners.
retro.terminal.title: Retro Terminal
retro.terminal.summary: A complete CRT-style command terminal built from UniGUI widgets, a custom AdminConsole, and a chained post-processing effect.
retro.terminal.section.result.title: What you are building
retro.terminal.section.result.body:
This guide rebuilds `RetroTerminalScreen` as a portable `UniScreen`. It covers the screen factory, full-size widget tree, `AdminConsole` customization, typed command registration, and a CRT shader chain.

For reproducible captures in `TestMod`, click **Retro Wiki** on the title or pause screen. Use `Ctrl+Alt+F1` for the base screen, `Ctrl+Alt+F2` for the layered root, `Ctrl+Alt+F3` for the console, `Ctrl+Alt+F4` for command output, `Ctrl+Alt+F5` for autocomplete, and `Ctrl+Alt+F6` for the effects preset.
retro.terminal.section.screen.title: 1. Create the screen
retro.terminal.section.screen.body:
Start with `DefaultUIContext` and a `UnityLikeUIScaleProvider`. The scale provider keeps the terminal readable across different window sizes. Return a `UniScreen` instead of opening it inside the factory; this keeps construction testable and lets the host decide when to call `openGui()`.

![Finished retro terminal screen](<../../../assets/demos/retro-terminal/01-screen.png>)
retro.terminal.section.tree.title: 2. Build the widget tree
retro.terminal.section.tree.body:
Use a full-size `StackPanel` for the scene, then add a background, a vignette border, and the console as separate layers. The `OverlayLayer` is the root returned by the screen. Layout is expressed with percentage sizes, padding, and flex rules; no Minecraft coordinates are required.

![Layered terminal root](<../../../assets/demos/retro-terminal/02-layered-root.png>)
retro.terminal.section.console.title: 3. Customize AdminConsole
retro.terminal.section.console.body:
Subclass `AdminConsole` when the standard command console needs a visual identity. Override the configuration hooks for the root, header, prompt, input field, output labels, completion popup, and scroll view. Keep lifecycle behavior in the base class and change only the visual or content-specific parts.

![Customized console](<../../../assets/demos/retro-terminal/03-console.png>)
retro.terminal.section.commands.title: 4. Register commands
retro.terminal.section.commands.body:
Register simple commands with `registerCommand`, and use `AdminCommandRegistry.command(...)` when a command needs typed arguments and suggestions. The terminal example defines `status`, `scan`, `players`, and `teleport`; command callbacks append lines through the console API instead of directly touching the renderer.

![Terminal command output](<../../../assets/demos/retro-terminal/02-commands.png>)

![Terminal command completion popup](<../../../assets/demos/retro-terminal/03-autocomplete.png>)
retro.terminal.section.effects.title: 5. Add the CRT effect
retro.terminal.section.effects.body:
Wrap the widget root in `PostProcessingLayer` and assign a `UiPostEffectChain` containing the terminal, bloom, and frame shader passes. Uniforms are configured when the screen is created; the UI tree remains independent from the backend that executes the passes. The selected host backend must implement post-processing, and the host project must package the three shader resources named by the passes.

![CRT post-processing effect](<../../../assets/demos/retro-terminal/04-effects.png>)

panel.widget.title: PanelWidget
panel.widget.summary: Base container for multi-child widgets managing hierarchy, deferred mutations, and rendering order.
panel.widget.section.overview.title: Overview
panel.widget.section.overview.body:
`PanelWidget` is the abstract foundation for all multi-child containers in UniGUI. It manages child widget ownership, assigns parent links, propagates `UIContext`, and handles deferred mutation queues so adding or removing children during event or render passes is safe.

By default, `PanelWidget` lays out ordinary children like a stack/overlay within its content bounds, while out-of-flow absolute children are positioned via `AbsoluteLayoutEngine`.
panel.widget.section.mutations.title: Deferred Mutations & Snapshotting
panel.widget.section.mutations.body:
- **Deferred Queue**: Mutations triggered via `addChild()`, `removeChild()`, and `clearChildren()` are queued and applied during `applyQueuedMutations()` before layout and render passes.
- **Array Snapshot**: Traversal passes use a cached `childSnapshot()` array, avoiding iterator allocations in hot tick and render loops.
- **Z-Order & Culling**: Children are sorted according to `ZOrder` and culled against scissor/render clip boundaries.
panel.widget.example.basic.title: Managing Children
panel.widget.method.add_child.title: Add child
panel.widget.method.add_child.summary: Queues a child widget for addition at the end of the children list.
panel.widget.method.remove_child.title: Remove child
panel.widget.method.remove_child.summary: Queues a child widget for removal from this container.
panel.widget.method.clear_children.title: Clear children
panel.widget.method.clear_children.summa: Queues removal and disposal of all child widgets.
surface.widget.title: SurfaceWidget
surface.widget.summary: Container with a composable Surface: background colors, multi-layer textures, shaders, borders, and corner radius.
surface.widget.section.overview.title: Overview
surface.widget.section.overview.body:
`SurfaceWidget` is the foundation of UniGUI's modern styling system. Instead of hardcoding a specific renderer class, every `SurfaceWidget` embeds a composable `Surface`.

The background source can be a solid color, texture, or procedural GLSL shader, and can be switched dynamically via code, XML, or Theme/StylePack selectors without replacing the widget or renderer.
surface.widget.section.layers.title: Textures & Overlay Layers
surface.widget.section.layers.body:
- **Base Background**: Configured via `background(color)`, `backgroundTexture(handle)`, or `backgroundShader(handle)`.
- **Nine-Slice Slicing**: Enable via `backgroundTextureFit(ImageFit.NINE_SLICE)` and `sliceBorders(n)` for scalable panels without corner distortion.
- **Overlay Textures**: Add multiple layered textures over the background via `overlayTexture(handle)`. Each layer supports individual tint, source UVs, and fit modes.
- **Transitions & Animation**: Visual properties such as `backgroundColor`, `borderColor`, `borderWidth`, and `radius` can be smoothly transitioned using `animateBackgroundColor(...)`, `animateRadius(...)`, etc.
surface.widget.example.card.title: Configured Surface Card
surface.widget.method.background.title: Set Background
surface.widget.method.background.summary: Sets background fill color and automatically enables background visibility.
surface.widget.method.border.title: Set Border
surface.widget.method.border.summary: Sets border stroke color and automatically enables border visibility.
surface.widget.method.border_width.title: Set border width
surface.widget.method.border_width.summa: Sets the thickness of the border stroke in UI pixels.
surface.widget.method.radius.title: Set corner radius
surface.widget.method.radius.summary: Sets uniform corner radius in UI pixels.
box.title: Box
box.summary: Standard styled container combining background color, texture, shader, border, radius, and child layout.
box.section.overview.title: Overview
box.section.overview.body:
`Box` is the standard concrete visual container in UniGUI. It extends `SurfaceWidget<Box>` and has surface rendering active by default.

Use `Box` whenever you need a styled card, panel, background wrapper, or modal container.
box.example.card.title: Card with Border and Radius
border.title: Border
border.summary: Render-only decorative outline widget without child widgets.
border.section.overview.title: Overview
border.section.overview.body:
`Border` is a lightweight, render-only decorative outline widget without child widgets. It is useful as a standalone overlay layer — for example, to draw an active selection outline, highlight bounds during debugging, or draw decorative frames.

If you need a container with background, border, and nested children, prefer `Box`.
border.example.outline.title: Selection Outline
border.method.thickness.title: Set thickness
border.method.thickness.summary: Sets border stroke thickness in UI pixels.
border.method.radius.title: Set radius
border.method.radius.summary: Sets corner radius in UI pixels.
linear.box.title: LinearBox
linear.box.summary: One-dimensional flex container arranging children sequentially along a main axis without wrapping.
linear.box.section.overview.title: Overview
linear.box.section.overview.body:
`LinearBox` is a 1D flex container that synchronizes its `orientation` and `spacing` with its internal `LayoutStyle`. Horizontal orientation maps to `FlexDirection.ROW` with `columnGap`, while vertical orientation maps to `FlexDirection.COLUMN` with `rowGap`.

For common fixed-orientation layouts, prefer `VBox` (vertical) or `HBox` (horizontal). Use `LinearBox` directly when the orientation axis must change dynamically at runtime.
linear.box.section.surface.title: Opt-in Visual Surface
linear.box.section.surface.body: `LinearBox` inherits `SurfaceWidget`, meaning backgrounds, borders, and textures are supported. To preserve transparency by default, surface rendering is initially disabled (`boxVisualEnabled=false`). The first call to `background(color)` or `border(color)` automatically enables surface rendering.
linear.box.example.basic.title: Dynamic Orientation Row
vbox.title: VBox
vbox.summary: Vertical linear container stacking children top-to-bottom with uniform spacing.
vbox.section.overview.title: Overview
vbox.section.overview.body:
`VBox` is a vertical shorthand for `LinearBox`. It arranges child widgets from top to bottom using flex layout (`FlexDirection.COLUMN`) without line wrapping.

Spacing between adjacent elements is configured with `spacing(pixels)` and updates `rowGap`. Individual children can request flex expansion via `child.layout(s -> s.expand())`.
vbox.example.form.title: Vertical Form Layout
hbox.title: HBox
hbox.summary: Horizontal linear container placing children left-to-right with uniform spacing.
hbox.section.overview.title: Overview
hbox.section.overview.body:
`HBox` is a horizontal shorthand for `LinearBox`. It arranges child widgets from left to right using flex layout (`FlexDirection.ROW`) without line wrapping.

Spacing between adjacent elements is configured with `spacing(pixels)` and updates `columnGap`. Ideal for toolbars, button rows, navigation bars, and inline controls.
hbox.example.toolbar.title: Horizontal Toolbar
flex.box.title: FlexBox
flex.box.summary: CSS-like flex container configured directly via LayoutStyle flexbox properties.
flex.box.section.overview.title: Overview
flex.box.section.overview.body:
`FlexBox` is the direct UniGUI equivalent to CSS `display: flex`. Unlike `LinearBox` and `WrapPanel`, it does not store secondary orientation or spacing states.

Everything — direction, wrapping, main-axis justification (`justifyContent`), cross-axis alignment (`alignItems`), and item gaps (`rowGap`, `columnGap`) — is configured directly on its `layoutStyle()`.
flex.box.example.advanced.title: Flex Justification & Alignment
grid.box.title: GridBox
grid.box.summary: Multi-column grid container placing children into uniform cells or custom track templates.
grid.box.section.overview.title: Overview
grid.box.section.overview.body:
`GridBox` arranges children in a two-dimensional grid. By default, it splits available width into a fixed number of uniform columns (`columns(n)`) and lays out children sequentially in row-major order.

Spacing can be configured globally via `spacing(px)` or independently via `horizontalSpacing(px)` and `verticalSpacing(px)`.

For complex tracks (proportional `fr`, pixel `px`, or `minmax`), assign custom track templates with `gridColumns(GridTrack...)`.
grid.box.example.basic.title: Inventory Grid
stack.panel.title: StackPanel
stack.panel.summary: Overlay container stacking all children within a shared rectangular slot.
stack.panel.section.overview.title: Overview
stack.panel.section.overview.body:
`StackPanel` is an overlay container where every non-collapsed child is placed in the same shared rectangular slot. Each child is aligned according to its own margin, preferred size, and alignment rules (`Alignment.STRETCH`, `CENTER`, etc.).

This makes `StackPanel` ideal for composition: layering decorative backdrops, content, notification badges, or watermark overlays on top of one another.
stack.panel.example.badge.title: Overlay Badge over Avatar
wrap.panel.title: WrapPanel
wrap.panel.summary: Flow container wrapping children to a new row or column when space is exceeded.
wrap.panel.section.overview.title: Overview
wrap.panel.section.overview.body:
`WrapPanel` is a multi-line flow container (`FlexWrap.WRAP`). In horizontal orientation, children flow left-to-right and wrap onto new lines when the container boundary is reached. In vertical orientation, children flow top-to-bottom and wrap into new columns.

- **`spacing(px)`**: Distance between items within the same line.
- **`lineSpacing(px)`**: Distance between consecutive wrapped lines.
wrap.panel.example.chips.title: Tag Chip Cloud
scroll.view.title: ScrollView
scroll.view.desc: A scroll viewport container that hosts a single content widget and manages horizontal and vertical scrolling.
scroll.view.overview: ScrollView provides a scrollable viewport for content that exceeds visible panel bounds. Scrolling can be configured along X and Y axes via overflow settings (Overflow.AUTO, Overflow.SCROLL, Overflow.HIDDEN). It supports mouse wheel scrolling with Shift modifier toggling horizontal axis, clamp bounds, and fine-grained scroll step customization.
scroll.view.bars: Scrollbars can operate in overlay mode (floating on top of content with interactive hover effect) or reserved mode (allocating dedicated screen space for scrollbar tracks). You can customize track colors, thumb colors, thumb hover colors, track thickness, and gap between viewport and bars.
scroll.view.methods: Programmatic scrolling is performed using scrollTo(x, y) and scrollBy(dx, dy). The scroll position is automatically clamped between 0 and maximum allowable scroll extent. You can also dynamically enable or disable scrolling via scrollingEnabled(boolean).
scroll.view.example.basic: Basic Scroll View with Vertical Overflow
scroll.view.method.content: Sets the single content widget inside the viewport.
scroll.view.param.content: the widget to display in the viewport
scroll.view.method.scroll_to: Scrolls to absolute coordinates (x, y), clamped to valid bounds.
scroll.view.method.scroll_by: Scrolls relative to current position by dx and dy.
scroll.view.method.scroll_step: Sets the scroll step multiplier in UI pixels per wheel delta unit.
scroll.view.method.overlay_scrollbars: Controls whether scrollbars overlay content or reserve layout space.
scroll.view.param.overlay_scrollbars: true for overlay mode, false for reserved mode
dock.panel.title: DockPanel
dock.panel.desc: A layout panel that arranges child widgets along outer edges (left, right, top, bottom), allocating remaining space to the last child.
dock.panel.overview: DockPanel sequentially lays out each child along one of the outer edges defined by DockSide. Each docked child consumes space along that side, shrinking the remaining rectangular area for subsequent children. When lastChildFill is true (default), the final child fills the remaining central area regardless of its dock side.
dock.panel.sides: The DockSide enum defines four docking edges: LEFT, RIGHT, TOP, and BOTTOM. The order in which children are added determines which edge has priority when shrinking the available rectangle.
dock.panel.fill: DockPanel is designed for edge-based screen layouts (such as toolbars, headers, status bars, and central workspaces). For advanced docking with detachable floating windows, split docking zones, and tabbed docking, use DockingRoot and DockingManager instead.
dock.panel.method.add_child: Adds a child widget docked to a specific edge.
dock.panel.param.dock_side: the edge to dock the child against
dock.panel.method.dock_side: Gets or sets the dock side for a child widget.
dock.panel.method.last_child_fill: Controls whether the last child expands to fill all remaining interior space.
dock.panel.param.last_child_fill: true to make the last child fill remaining area
split.panel.title: SplitPanel
split.panel.desc: A two-pane container divided by an interactive, draggable splitter handle.
split.panel.overview: SplitPanel manages two child widget slots: first and second. An internal interactive Splitter widget is positioned between them, allowing the user to resize the two sections via mouse dragging.
split.panel.orientation: The panel supports both horizontal (Orientation.HORIZONTAL - first slot left, second slot right) and vertical (Orientation.VERTICAL - first slot top, second slot bottom) splitting. Minimum dimensions for both slots can be enforced via minFirstSize(float) and minSecondSize(float).
split.panel.ratio: The division of space is specified by splitRatio (ranging from 0.0 to 1.0), representing the proportion of available space assigned to the first slot. During user interaction, the splitter captures mouse pointer events and smoothly updates the ratio while respecting minimum size boundaries.
split.panel.example.basic: Horizontal Split with Sidebar and Editor
split.panel.method.first: Sets the widget in the first slot (left or top).
split.panel.method.second: Sets the widget in the second slot (right or bottom).
split.panel.method.orientation: Sets the split axis orientation (horizontal or vertical).
split.panel.method.split_ratio: Sets the fraction of available space allocated to the first slot (clamped to 0.0..1.0).
split.panel.method.min_first_size: Sets the minimum pixel size for the first slot.
split.panel.method.min_second_size: Sets the minimum pixel size for the second slot.
panel.row.widget.title: PanelRowWidget
panel.row.widget.desc: A two-sided row container that aligns widgets to the left and right edges with configurable heights and gaps.
panel.row.widget.overview: PanelRowWidget is designed for headers, toolbars, title bars, and form rows. It maintains two distinct widget groups: left-aligned (stacked left-to-right) and right-aligned (stacked right-to-left). Both groups participate in layout calculations while keeping a clear separation between primary actions/titles and secondary controls.
panel.row.widget.sizing: The overall row height is configured with rowHeight(float). Inter-element spacing can be fine-tuned via gap(float), leftGap(float), and rightGap(float). Slot widths can be fixed using leftWidth(float) and rightWidth(float) or left automatic (LayoutConstraints.AUTO).
panel.row.widget.slots: Widgets can be added one-by-one via addLeft(Widget) and addRight(Widget), or single widgets can be set directly via left(Widget) and right(Widget), which automatically clear any previous widgets on that side.
panel.row.widget.example.toolbar: Custom Toolbar Row with Multiple Controls
panel.row.widget.method.left: Replaces the entire left group with a single widget.
panel.row.widget.param.left: the widget for the left side
panel.row.widget.method.right: Replaces the entire right group with a single widget.
panel.row.widget.param.right: the widget for the right side
panel.row.widget.method.add_left: Appends a widget to the left-aligned group.
panel.row.widget.method.add_right: Appends a widget to the right-aligned group.
panel.row.widget.method.row_height: Sets the preferred height of the row.
panel.row.widget.method.gap: Sets uniform spacing between elements on both sides and between groups.
setting.row.title: SettingRow
setting.row.desc: A specialized configuration row with a label on the left and an interactive control widget on the right.
setting.row.overview: SettingRow is a specialized subclass of PanelRowWidget created specifically for settings dialogs, preference panes, and option forms. The left slot hosts an integrated Label, while the right slot contains the interactive control (such as a Slider, Checkbox, Dropdown, or TextField).
setting.row.focus: A key usability feature of SettingRow is automatic focus redirection: the left Label is configured with label.focusTarget(control), so clicking on the label automatically passes keyboard and pointer focus to the associated control.
setting.row.customization: You can customize the label using plain text via labelText(String) or formatted RichText via labelText(RichText). The control width can be fixed via controlWidth(float), and standard row height and gaps are fully configurable.
setting.row.example.basic: Creating a Setting Row for a Slider Control
setting.row.example.list: List of Setting Rows in a Settings Dialog
setting.row.method.control: Sets the interactive control widget on the right side.
setting.row.param.control: the control widget (e.g. Slider, Toggle, TextField)
setting.row.method.label_text: Sets the plain-text title for the setting label.
setting.row.method.control_width: Sets a fixed width for the right control slot.
setting.row.method.label: Returns the underlying Label instance for advanced text styling.
view.title: View
view.desc: A card-like container combining Box visual styling with an integrated title label and vertical content layout.
view.overview: View extends Box to provide a ready-to-use card or panel container. It automatically initializes an internal VBox containing a header Label and a flexible content area. It is widely used in debug screens, demo panels, and HUD cards.
view.styling: Because View extends Box, it inherits full visual background rendering (solid color, gradient, textures), borders, corner radiuses, and shadows. Default styling is loaded from WidgetStyles.View.DEFAULT.
view.content: Widgets should be added via addContent(Widget) or directly into content(). These widgets are arranged vertically below the title label with default margins and spacing.
view.example.dialog: Card Panel with Title and Action Content
view.method.title: Sets the text of the header label.
view.param.title: title text string
view.method.content: Returns the internal VBox container hosting the content widgets.
view.method.add_content: Appends a widget to the internal vertical content container below the title.
view.param.widget: widget to append to view content
scroll.view.summary: Scrollable viewport container hosting a single content widget with horizontal and vertical scroll support.
scroll.view.section.overview.title: Overview
scroll.view.section.overview.body: ScrollView provides a scrollable viewport for content that exceeds visible panel bounds. Scrolling can be configured along X and Y axes via overflow settings (`Overflow.AUTO`, `Overflow.SCROLL`, `Overflow.HIDDEN`). It supports mouse wheel scrolling with Shift modifier toggling horizontal axis, clamp bounds, and fine-grained scroll step customization.
scroll.view.section.bars.title: Scrollbar Modes & Styling
scroll.view.section.bars.body: Scrollbars can operate in overlay mode (floating on top of content with interactive hover effect) or reserved mode (allocating dedicated screen space for scrollbar tracks). You can customize track colors, thumb colors, thumb hover colors, track thickness, and gap between viewport and bars.
scroll.view.example.basic.title: Basic ScrollView with Overflow
dock.panel.summary: Edge-docking layout container arranging child widgets along outer boundaries (left, right, top, bottom).
dock.panel.section.overview.title: Overview
dock.panel.section.overview.body: DockPanel sequentially lays out each child along one of the outer edges defined by `DockSide`. Each docked child consumes space along that side, shrinking the remaining rectangular area for subsequent children.
dock.panel.section.fill.title: Last Child Fill
dock.panel.section.fill.body: When `lastChildFill` is true (default), the final child widget occupies the entire remaining interior area. For complex IDE docking (tear-off windows, tabs, split docking zones), use `DockingRoot` and `DockingManager` instead of `DockPanel`.
dock.panel.example.shell.title: Application Shell Layout
split.panel.summary: Two-pane container separated by an interactive draggable splitter for dynamic resizing.
split.panel.section.overview.title: Overview
split.panel.section.overview.body: SplitPanel manages two child widget slots: `first` and `second`. An internal interactive `Splitter` widget is positioned between them, allowing the user to resize the two sections via mouse dragging.
split.panel.section.resizing.title: Orientation & Constraints
split.panel.section.resizing.body: The panel supports both horizontal (`Orientation.HORIZONTAL` - first slot left, second slot right) and vertical (`Orientation.VERTICAL` - first slot top, second slot bottom) splitting. Space division is specified by `splitRatio` (0.0 to 1.0) and constrained by `minFirstSize` and `minSecondSize`.
split.panel.example.basic.title: Horizontal Split Panel
panel.row.widget.summary: Two-sided row container organizing widgets into left-aligned and right-aligned groups.
panel.row.widget.section.overview.title: Overview
panel.row.widget.section.overview.body: PanelRowWidget is designed for headers, toolbars, title bars, and form rows. It maintains two distinct widget groups: left-aligned (stacked left-to-right) and right-aligned (stacked right-to-left). Both groups participate in layout calculations while keeping a clear separation between primary actions/titles and secondary controls.
panel.row.widget.section.alignment.title: Sizing & Spacing
panel.row.widget.section.alignment.body: The overall row height is configured with `rowHeight(float)`. Inter-element spacing can be fine-tuned via `gap(float)`, `leftGap(float)`, and `rightGap(float)`. Slot widths can be fixed using `leftWidth(float)` and `rightWidth(float)` or left automatic (`LayoutConstraints.AUTO`).
panel.row.widget.example.toolbar.title: Toolbar Row Layout
setting.row.summary: Specialized settings row holding a label on the left and an interactive control on the right.
setting.row.section.overview.title: Overview
setting.row.section.overview.body: SettingRow is a specialized subclass of `PanelRowWidget` created specifically for settings dialogs, preference panes, and option forms. The left slot hosts an integrated `Label`, while the right slot contains the interactive control (such as a Slider, Checkbox, Dropdown, or TextField).
setting.row.section.focus.title: Focus Redirection
setting.row.section.focus.body: A key usability feature of SettingRow is automatic focus redirection: the left `Label` is configured with `label.focusTarget(control)`, so clicking on the label automatically passes keyboard and pointer focus to the associated control.
setting.row.example.basic.title: Volume Setting Row
view.summary: Card-like visual container embedding a header Label and a vertical VBox content area.
view.section.overview.title: Overview
view.section.overview.body: View extends `Box` to provide a ready-to-use card or panel container. It automatically initializes an internal `VBox` containing a header `Label` and a flexible content area. It is widely used in debug screens, demo panels, and HUD cards.
view.section.card.title: Styling & Structure
view.section.card.body: Because View extends `Box`, it inherits full visual background rendering (solid color, gradient, textures), borders, corner radiuses, and shadows. Default styling is loaded from `WidgetStyles.View.DEFAULT`.
view.example.basic.title: Creating an Inspector Card

dock.side.title: DockSide
dock.side.summary: Specifies which outer boundary edge (LEFT, RIGHT, TOP, BOTTOM) a child widget docks against in a DockPanel.
dock.side.section.overview.title: Overview
dock.side.section.overview.body:
`DockSide` defines the four peripheral boundary edges used by `DockPanel` to pin child widgets:

- **`LEFT`**: Pins the child against the left boundary of the remaining area.
- **`RIGHT`**: Pins the child against the right boundary.
- **`TOP`**: Pins the child against the top boundary.
- **`BOTTOM`**: Pins the child against the bottom boundary.

Note: `DockSide` is specific to the lightweight `DockPanel` layout container. For complete IDE-style docking (tear-off windows, tabs, docking drop targets), use `DockArea` and `DockingManager`.

button.title: Button
button.summary: Standard interactive push button with composable surface, icon, text, and rich state transitions.
button.section.overview.title: Overview
button.section.overview.body:
`Button` extends `SurfaceWidget<Button>` to combine a styled background plate (solid color, texture, or GLSL shader), border, corner radius, focus ring, and centered foreground text/icon.

It supports reactive state styling (`WidgetState.NORMAL`, `HOVERED`, `PRESSED`, `DISABLED`), pointer capture, keypress activation (`SPACE`, `ENTER`), and fluent event subscription via `onClick(...)`.
button.section.states.title: Hover and Pressed Chrome
button.section.states.body:
Buttons can specify explicit per-state overrides that supersede theme defaults:

- **`hoverBackground(color)`**: Dedicated background color when hovered.
- **`pressedBackground(color)`**: Dedicated background color while pressed.
- **`hoverTexture(handle)` / `pressedTexture(handle)`**: Specialized state textures.
- **`hoverShader(handle)`**: Animated procedural GLSL shader active on hover.
- **`interactionTransitions(true)`**: Enables smooth spring-like scale and opacity feedback on hover and press.

code.editor.title: CodeEditor
code.editor.summary: Rich code editor widget supporting syntax highlighting, diagnostics, line numbers, and autocompletion.
code.editor.section.overview.title: Overview
code.editor.section.overview.body: `CodeEditor` extends `TextArea` to provide a full-featured code editor. It integrates syntax tokenization via `CodeTokenizer`, static analysis diagnostics via `CodeValidator`, and intelligent code completion via `CompletionProvider`.
code.editor.example.basic.title: Basic CodeEditor Setup
code.editor.method.language_preset.title: Set Language Preset
code.editor.method.language_preset.summa: Applies tokenizer and validator configurations from language preset.

code.editor.method.validator.title: Set Validator
code.editor.method.line_numbers.title: Show Line Numbers
code.editor.method.line_numbers.summary: Toggles display of gutter line numbers.
code.editor.method.dirty.title: Is Dirty
code.editor.method.dirty.summary: Returns true if editor text has unsaved changes.
code.editor.method.mark_clean.title: Mark Clean
code.editor.method.mark_clean.summary: Resets dirty state marker after saving text.
xml.code.editor.title: XmlCodeEditor
xml.code.editor.summary: Specialized XML and UI layout code editor with schema validation, formatting, and tag autocompletion.
xml.code.editor.section.overview.title: Overview
xml.code.editor.section.overview.body: `XmlCodeEditor` extends `CodeEditor` configured specifically for UniGUI XML layout files. Includes built-in XML parsing, hierarchy formatting, widget registry autocompletion, and XML syntax error squiggles.
xml.code.editor.example.basic.title: XML Layout Editor
xml.code.editor.method.registry.title: Set Widget Registry
xml.code.editor.method.registry.summary: Sets widget registry used for tag autocompletion and attribute schema validation.
xml.code.editor.method.validate_xml.summ: Executes synchronous XML schema and syntax validation.
xml.code.editor.method.format_xml.title: Format XML
xml.code.editor.method.format_xml.summar: Formats XML source with standard indentation and attribute line wrapping.
code.language.preset.title: CodeLanguagePreset
code.language.preset.summary: Enumeration of built-in language presets for syntax highlighting and validation.
code.language.preset.section.overview.bo: `CodeLanguagePreset` defines standard language identifiers (such as `XML`, `JSON`, `GLSL`, `JAVASCRIPT`) configured with default tokenizers and styles.
code.language.presets.title: CodeLanguagePresets
code.language.presets.summary: Factory registry supplying tokenizers and validators for language presets.
code.language.presets.section.overview.b: `CodeLanguagePresets` provides static helper methods to apply preconfigured tokenizer and validator pipelines to a `CodeEditor`.
code.language.presets.method.apply.title: Apply Preset
code.language.presets.method.apply.summa: Applies tokenizer, validator, and styles corresponding to language preset.
code.tokenizer.title: CodeTokenizer
code.tokenizer.summary: Functional interface converting source code text into colored syntax tokens.
code.tokenizer.section.overview.title: Overview
code.tokenizer.section.overview.body: Implementations of `CodeTokenizer` scan editor text in a `CodeTokenizationContext` and emit a list of `CodeToken` ranges for syntax rendering.
code.tokenizer.method.tokenize.title: Tokenize Text
code.tokenizer.method.tokenize.summary: Parses text into list of styled syntax tokens.
code.token.title: CodeToken
code.token.summary: Immutable range token associating character indices with a TokenStyle.
code.token.section.overview.title: Overview
code.token.section.overview.body: `CodeToken` holds `startIndex`, `endIndex`, and a `TokenStyle` specifying font color and decoration for a highlighted span of code.
token.style.title: TokenStyle
token.style.summary: Visual styling descriptor for syntax tokens including foreground color.
token.style.section.overview.title: Overview
token.style.section.overview.body: `TokenStyle` wraps a `ColorView` applied to characters matching a syntax token.
code.validator.title: CodeValidator
code.validator.summary: Functional interface performing static analysis and reporting code diagnostics.
code.validator.section.overview.title: Overview
code.validator.section.overview.body: `CodeValidator` inspects document contents and returns a collection of `CodeDiagnostic` objects indicating errors, warnings, or hints.
code.validator.method.validate.title: Validate Code
code.validator.method.validate.summary: Analyzes code within validation context and returns diagnostics.
code.diagnostic.title: CodeDiagnostic
code.diagnostic.summary: Diagnostic report entry representing an error, warning, or hint at a specific code range.
code.diagnostic.section.overview.title: Overview
code.diagnostic.section.overview.body: `CodeDiagnostic` captures diagnostic severity, message, line, column, and character offsets to render squiggles and tooltip notices.
completion.provider.title: CompletionProvider
completion.provider.summary: Interface producing autocompletion proposals based on editor cursor context.
completion.provider.section.overview.bod: `CompletionProvider` inspects the document text and caret offset in `CompletionContext` to generate a list of candidate `CompletionItem` choices.
completion.provider.method.complete.summ: Generates completion items for current cursor context.
completion.item.title: CompletionItem
completion.item.summary: Individual autocompletion suggestion with rich label, insertion text, and replacement range.
completion.item.section.overview.title: Overview
completion.item.section.overview.body: `CompletionItem` represents one autocomplete suggestion in the popup list, specifying what text will be inserted into the editor when selected.
completion.context.title: CompletionContext
completion.context.summary: Context record supplied to completion providers containing editor text and cursor position.
completion.context.section.overview.body: `CompletionContext` encapsulates full document text, caret index, line, column, and trigger character for autocompletion queries.
code.tokenization.context.title: CodeTokenizationContext
code.tokenization.context.summary: Context record passed to syntax tokenizers containing source text and language ID.
code.tokenization.context.section.overvi: `CodeTokenizationContext` provides the input string and target language identifier needed during syntax parsing.
code.validation.context.title: CodeValidationContext
code.validation.context.summary: Context record passed to code validators containing document text and language ID.
code.validation.context.section.overview: `CodeValidationContext` supplies document source code and language identifier for static analysis.
admin.console.title: AdminConsole
admin.console.summary: Interactive developer and administrative console widget with command execution and log output.
admin.console.section.overview.title: Overview
admin.console.section.overview.body: `AdminConsole` provides an in-game terminal for debugging and executing commands. It integrates command autocompletion via `AdminCommandRegistry`, command history navigation, and colored log scrolling.
admin.console.example.basic.title: Admin Console Setup

admin.command.registry.title: AdminCommandRegistry
admin.command.registry.summary: Central registry for console commands with argument completion, alias resolution, and handlers.
`AdminCommandRegistry` manages registered commands, dispatches execution, and calculates parameter autocompletions for `AdminConsole`.

virtual.table.column.title: VirtualTableColumn
virtual.table.column.summary: Column configuration for VirtualTableView defining header text, width, alignments, and overflow mode.
virtual.table.column.section.overview.bo: `VirtualTableColumn` is an immutable record configuring a column within a `VirtualTableView`. It specifies the plain or RichText header, width, horizontal and vertical content alignments, and text clipping behavior.
virtual.table.column.example.basic.title: Defining Table Columns

virtual.table.view.title: VirtualTableView
virtual.table.view.summary: High-performance virtualized grid/table view widget supporting column resizing, reordering, sorting, and cell editing.
virtual.table.view.section.overview.body: `VirtualTableView` renders large tabular data sets with high performance by virtualizing rows. Features draggable column headers, column resizing, interactive sort indicators, cell selection models, keyboard navigation, and inline cell editing.
virtual.table.view.example.basic.title: Basic Table Setup

text.widget.title: TextWidget
text.widget.summary: Abstract foundation widget for text rendering components supporting plain strings, RichText, fonts, colors, and gradients.
text.widget.section.overview.title: Overview
text.widget.section.overview.body: `TextWidget` serves as the base class for `Label`, `Text`, `TextBlock`, and `RichTextView`. It encapsulates font selection, font pixel size, plain text and `RichText` models, color gradients, and text layout measurement.
text.widget.example.basic.title: Configuring TextWidget

text.widget.method.text_gradient.title: Set Text Gradient
text.widget.method.text_gradient.summary: Applies two-color linear gradient to rendered text glyphs.
label.title: Label
label.summary: Text caption widget associated with an interactive focus target control or form input.
label.section.overview.title: Overview
label.section.overview.body: `Label` displays single-line or wrapped text captions. When clicked, it automatically transfers input focus to its associated `focusTarget` control (such as a `TextField` or `Checkbox`), improving form accessibility.
label.example.basic.title: Associated Form Label
label.method.focus_target.title: Focus Target

label.method.wrap.title: Set Text Wrapping
label.method.wrap.summary: Enables or disables automatic multi-line text wrapping.
text.display.title: Text
text.display.summary: Lightweight text display widget for static or dynamic strings and RichText.
text.display.section.overview.title: Overview
text.display.section.overview.body: `Text` is a lightweight display component extending `TextWidget`. Unlike `Label`, it does not handle focus delegation, making it ideal for headers, read-only stats, and notifications.
text.display.example.basic.title: Simple Text Widget
text.display.example.basic.code:

        .color(Color.YELLOW);
text.block.title: TextBlock
text.block.summary: Multiline paragraph text display widget supporting line wrapping, line height, and text alignments.
text.block.section.overview.title: Overview
text.block.section.overview.body: `TextBlock` is optimized for displaying longer narrative paragraphs, documentation excerpts, and multi-line descriptions with configurable line spacing and paragraph alignment.
text.block.example.basic.title: Paragraph TextBlock
rich.text.view.title: RichTextView
rich.text.view.summary: Formatted rich text widget rendering styled runs, inline icons, color spans, and links.
rich.text.view.section.overview.title: Overview
rich.text.view.section.overview.body: `RichTextView` renders composite `RichText` objects containing multiple styled spans, bold/italic text, colored badges, inline texture icons, and clickable URL links.
rich.text.view.example.basic.title: Displaying RichText
separator.title: Separator
separator.summary: Horizontal or vertical divider line widget for visually grouping interface sections.
separator.section.overview.title: Overview
separator.section.overview.body: `Separator` draws a clean divider line along either horizontal or vertical orientation. Useful for demarcating menu items, toolbars, and section boundaries.
separator.example.basic.title: Divider Line

shape.section.overview.title: Overview

path.widget.title: Path
path.widget.summary: Vector path widget drawing complex custom 2D shapes, bezier curves, and polylines.
path.widget.section.overview.title: Overview
path.widget.section.overview.body: `Path` renders arbitrary vector geometry described by `VectorPath`. Supports quadratic/cubic bezier curves, line segments, filled polygons, and stroke line caps.
path.widget.example.basic.title: Custom Vector Path
path.widget.method.path.title: Vector Path Model

texture.widget.title: TextureWidget
texture.widget.summary: Base widget for rendering textures, UV regions, nine-slice borders, and image handles.
texture.widget.section.overview.title: Overview
texture.widget.section.overview.body: `TextureWidget` displays textures represented by `TextureHandle`. Supports texture filtering modes (linear/nearest), wrap modes (clamp/repeat), mipmapping, and source UV coordinates.
texture.widget.example.basic.title: Rendering Texture
texture.widget.method.texture.title: Texture Handle
texture.widget.method.texture.summary: Returns or sets TextureHandle referenced by widget.

binding.keys.title: Signal Binding
binding.keys.summary: Connect widget properties to reusable typed signals with bidirectional updates.
binding.keys.section.overview.title: Binding model
binding.keys.section.overview.body:
Call `widget.bind(key, signal)` to connect a supported widget property to a signal. Binding is bidirectional: the signal's current value is applied immediately, later signal changes update the widget, and user edits update the signal. Built-in keys are `BindingKeys.TEXT` for `TextInput` and its subclasses, and `BindingKeys.CHECKED` for `ToggleButton` and its subclasses.

A key is matched by **object identity**, so declare a custom key once and reuse it: `static final BindingData<BooleanSignal> MY_CHECKBOX_VALUE = new BindingData<>(BooleanSignal.class);`. A custom `WidgetBase` subclass handles its keys in `createBinding(...)` and returns `null` for unknown keys. Unsupported keys are ignored; passing a source of the wrong type is an error. Rebinding the same key replaces the previous connection, and `WidgetBase.dispose()` closes active bindings.

Signal callbacks run synchronously on the thread that calls `set()`. Change UI-bound signals on the UI thread.

drag.outcome.section.overview.body:
`DragOutcome` represents the terminal resolution of an active drag-and-drop gesture.

### Outcome Values

| Value | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `DROPPED` | The payload was successfully dropped onto an accepting drop target zone. |
| `NO_TARGET` | The pointer was released over an area without an accepting drop target. |
| `CANCELLED` | The drag operation was explicitly cancelled or interrupted. |

!!! note "Lifecycle Completion"
    When `DragController` triggers `onDragEnd(Consumer<DragEnd>)`, the `DragEnd` object contains this outcome to let source widgets decide whether to remove items, reset styling, or revert animations.
drag.routed.event.section.overview.body:
`DragRoutedEvent` is the abstract base class for routed drag-and-drop notifications dispatched throughout the widget hierarchy.

### Routed Event Flow

| Phase | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `CAPTURING` | Dispatched from the root container downward toward the target widget under cursor. |
| `AT_TARGET` | Delivered directly to the candidate target widget beneath the pointer. |
| `BUBBLING` | Bubbles upwards from target back to the root widget. |

All drag events provide access to the active `DragSession`, transfer `DragPayload`, and pointer coordinates in root UI pixels.
drag.leave.event.section.overview.body:
`DragLeaveEvent` is dispatched to a drop zone when the pointer moves outside its bounding box or when the drag session is aborted.

Use this event to clear hover state highlights, remove placeholder items, or hide drop indicator lines.
drag.session.section.overview.body:
`DragSession` represents an active drag-and-drop interaction.

### Session Responsibilities

- **Pointer Tracking**: Manages root coordinates (`pointerX`, `pointerY`), press coordinates, and delta displacements (`deltaX`, `deltaY`).
- **Drop Target Coordination**: Tracks the current accepting `dropTarget()` widget.
- **Overlay Rendering**: Coordinates `DragGhost` rendering and insertion indicator rectangles (`showIndicator`, `clearIndicator`).
- **Autoscroll Integration**: Coordinates container autoscrolling when the pointer hovers near scrollable container edges.
drag.controller.section.overview.body:
`DragController` attaches drag initiator capabilities to any widget using composition.

### Usage Pattern

```java
DragController.attach(headerWidget)
        .dragged(entireCardWidget)
        .payload(() -> DragPayload.of("card-1", "cards/item", "Card 1"))
        .threshold(4.0f)
        .ghostWidget(entireCardWidget, 0.75f)
        .onDragEnd(end -> System.out.println("Result: " + end.outcome()));
```

### Configuration Options

| Option | Method | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Drag Handle | `attach(widget)` | The specific widget listening for pointer press events. |
| Dragged Widget | `dragged(widget)` | The logical component being moved (e.g. card container). |
| Lazy Payload | `payload(Supplier)` | Computes the payload only when the threshold is exceeded. |
| Threshold | `threshold(px)` | Deadzone in pixels before pointer movement triggers a drag. |
| Axis Lock | `lockGhostAxis(Orientation)` | Constrains ghost motion strictly horizontally or vertically. |
| Autoscroll | `autoScroll(edge, speed)` | Scrolls enclosing containers when dragging near boundaries. |
drop.controller.section.overview.body:
`DropController` provides drop target validation and lifecycle management for container widgets.

### Usage Pattern

```java
DropController.attach(targetContainer)
        .accepts("items/weapon", "items/armor")
        .onDragEnter(event -> targetContainer.style().border(ColorView.GREEN, 2.0f))
        .onDragLeave(event -> targetContainer.style().clearBorder())
        .onDrop(event -> addItem(event.payload().data(Item.class)));
```

### Features

- **Declarative Filtering**: Set allowed types via `accepts(String...)` or custom logic via `accepts(Predicate<DragPayload>)`.
- **Automatic Claiming**: Automatically calls `event.accept(zone)` when payload matches.
- **Lifecycle Callbacks**: Convenient chained handlers for `onDragEnter`, `onDragOver`, `onDragLeave`, and `onDrop`.
reorder.controller.section.overview.body:
`ReorderController` implements drag-to-reorder behavior for linear containers such as `VBox`, `HBox`, or `PanelWidget`.

### Features

- **Insertion Line Indicator**: Displays an animated insertion bar indicating where items will land.
- **Auto Apply**: Automatically mutates the container child list on drop when `autoApply(true)` is enabled.
- **Internal vs External**: Support reordering items from the same container only, or accepting foreign items matching payload filters.

```java
ReorderController.attach(vbox)
        .orientation(Orientation.VERTICAL)
        .accepts("task/*")
        .autoApply(true)
        .indicator(3.0f, 4.0f, ColorView.ofHex("#007ACC"))
        .onReorder((from, to) -> syncDatabaseOrder(from, to));
```
dock.pane.kind.section.overview.body:
`DockPaneKind` categorizes panes within an IDE layout.

| Kind | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `DOCUMENT` | Main editor documents (code files, canvas, diagrams) occupying central workspace nodes. |
| `TOOL` | Utility side panels (project explorer, console, terminal, inspector) docked around editors. |
`DockSplitOrientation` defines the direction a split dock node divides space between its two children.

| Orientation | Layout | Child 1 | Child 2 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `HORIZONTAL` | Side-by-side | Left | Right |
| `VERTICAL` | Stacked | Top | Bottom |
dock.policy.section.overview.body:
`DockPolicy` defines docking capabilities for window hosts.

| Policy | Dock Into Other Windows | Accept Foreign Panes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `FULL` | Yes | Yes |
| `GUEST_ONLY` | Yes | No |
| `DISABLED` | No | No |
dock.area.section.overview.body:
`DockArea` specifies target drop zones when docking a pane into an existing layout.

### Area Types

| DockArea | Action | Node Transformation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `CENTER` / `TAB` | Tab Grouping | Adds pane into the target leaf node as an additional tab. |
| `LEFT` | Split Horizontal | Divides target space: new pane on Left, existing on Right. |
| `RIGHT` | Split Horizontal | Divides target space: existing pane on Left, new on Right. |
| `TOP` | Split Vertical | Divides target space: new pane on Top, existing on Bottom. |
| `BOTTOM` | Split Vertical | Divides target space: existing pane on Top, new on Bottom. |
| `FLOAT` | Detach Window | Tears off pane into a separate floating window. |
dock.color.section.overview.body:
`DockColor` defines semantic color constants used throughout `DockTheme`.

Encompasses 44 distinct roles covering:
- **Tab Header**: Active, inactive, hovered, pinned, and close button colors.
- **Split Handles**: Normal, hover, and dragging bar accents.
- **Drop Previews**: Fill, stroke, and center cross indicators for dock targets.
- **Floating Chrome**: Window title bar, borders, shadows, and resize grips.
resize.grip.style.section.overview.body:
`ResizeGripStyle` renders the corner grab handle used to resize floating windows.

### Built-in Styles

| Preset | Visual Style |
| --- | --- |
| `ResizeGripStyle.TRIANGLE` | Solid or shaded corner triangle. |
| `ResizeGripStyle.LINES` | Diagonal textured grip ridges. |
dock.drag.controller.section.overview.bo:
`DockDragController` manages pointer drag gestures across docking tabs.

It computes hit tests against dock nodes, detects tear-offs when dragging outside dock bounds, evaluates cross-docking zones, and produces `DockDropIntent` previews.
dock.drop.intent.section.overview.body:
`DockDropIntent` represents a resolved target drop location during dock tab dragging.

Contains target `DockArea`, target pane ID, preview bounding rectangle, and whether the intent represents a split, tab grouping, or floating window tear-off.
dock.layout.snapshot.section.overview.bo:
`DockLayoutSnapshot` captures the complete recursive docking tree structure for persistence.

### Persistence Flow

1. Capture: `DockLayoutSnapshot snapshot = dockingManager.snapshot();`
2. Serialize: `String encoded = DockLayoutSnapshotCodec.encode(snapshot);`
3. Save: Persist `encoded` string into application settings or workspace file.
4. Restore: `dockingRoot.restoreLayout(snapshot, paneRegistry);`
dock.layout.snapshot.codec.section.overv:
`DockLayoutSnapshotCodec` serializes and deserializes `DockLayoutSnapshot` instances using the compact `DLS1` format.

Format handles recursive split nodes, split ratios, active tabs, and pane ID lists in a single string suitable for storage.
dock.node.section.overview.body:
`DockNode` is an immutable-like tree node structuring the docking hierarchy.

- **`LEAF` Node**: Holds a list of tabbed `DockPane`s with a `selectedIndex`.
- **`SPLIT` Node**: Divides two child nodes (`first`, `second`) along `HORIZONTAL` or `VERTICAL` orientation with a fractional `splitRatio`.
dock.pane.section.overview.body:
`DockPane` represents a dockable panel hosting arbitrary widget content.

### Key Capabilities

- **Header Customization**: Title, rich formatted text, and icons (`icon()`).
- **Dirty State**: `dirty(true)` renders an unsaved indicator (e.g. bullet point or accent).
- **Close Protection**: `onCloseRequested(guard)` prevents pane closing until confirmed or saved.
- **Classification**: Configurable as `DOCUMENT` or `TOOL`.
dock.theme.section.overview.body:
`DockTheme` configures all visual aspects of the docking subsystem.

### Factory Presets

| Theme Factory | Palette & Style |
| --- | --- |
| `DockTheme.defaultTheme()` | Standard dark IDE theme. |
| `DockTheme.editor()` | High-contrast code editor palette. |
| `DockTheme.classic()` | Clean light-mode palette. |

### Metrics & Styling

Configure tab height (`tabHeight`), corner radii (`tabRadius`), split handle thickness (`splitThickness`), floating window shadows, and resize grips.
docking.manager.section.overview.body:
`DockingManager` is the non-visual model and controller for docking layout trees.

Performs tree mutations:
- Adding panes to edge splits or tab groups (`addPane`, `tabPane`, `splitPane`).
- Reordering tabs within a leaf (`reorderPane`).
- Detaching panes to floating windows (`detachPaneForFloating`).
- Snapshot generation and restoration (`snapshot`, `restore`).
docking.root.section.overview.body:
`DockingRoot` is the top-level visual container integrating the entire docking system.

### Core Features

- Renders hierarchical split trees with draggable divider handles.
- Renders tab strips with close buttons, icons, and active indicators.
- Integrates with `WindowWidget` hosts for tear-off floating windows.
- Displays drop preview highlights and cross-docking targets.
- Dispatches docking lifecycle events (`onLayoutChanged`, `onDropPreviewChanged`).

post.processing.layer.section.overview.b:
`PostProcessingLayer` is a visual wrapper that intercepts rendering of its child content and applies post-processing shaders, effects, and custom scale factors.

Key capabilities:
- Custom shader and effect chains (`postEffect`, `effect`).
- Rendering scale manipulation (`effectScale`).
- Non-invasive wrapping of complex widget trees without affecting internal event propagation.
context.menu.section.overview.body:
`ContextMenu` is a floating dropdown menu container that presents an ordered list of actionable options, submenus, and visual separators.

Key features:
- Text and rich-text menu items with associated `Runnable` click handlers.
- Nested hierarchical submenus.
- Smart auto-repositioning to remain fully visible within host screen bounds (`hostBounds`, `arrangeInHost`).
- Dismissal on outside clicks (`closeOnOutsideClick`).
loading.indicator.section.overview.body:
`LoadingIndicator` provides dynamic visual feedback for ongoing background operations and asynchronous tasks.

Supported styles and modes:
- Multiple animation modes: `RING`, `BAR`, `PULSE`, `DOTS`.
- Fine-grained control over arc count, speed, phase, thickness, and size.
- Automatic animation tick integration when active.
notification.view.section.overview.body:
`NotificationView` manages a visual stack of transient notification banners and alert cards on top of application content.

Key features:
- Automatic positioning and stacking according to `Placement` (top-right, bottom-right, etc.).
- Animated entry, timed auto-dismissal, and exit transitions.
- Severity indicators, customizable icons, titles, and action buttons.
- Global and container-level hosting via `OverlayLayer`.
overlay.host.aware.section.overview.body:
`OverlayHostAware` is a functional contract implemented by floating widgets (such as tooltips, context menus, popups, and windows) to dynamically arrange and constrain their layout inside an overlay host's boundaries.

Primary method:
- `arrangeInHost(RectView hostBounds)`: Recalculates position, offsets, and dimensions to prevent clipping off-screen.
overlay.layer.section.overview.body:
`OverlayLayer` is a top-level container dedicated to rendering floating visual elements above standard UI widgets.

Responsibilities:
- Hosts popups, dropdowns, context menus, tooltips, and floating windows.
- Manages modal scrim dimming backdrops with customizable renderers and colors.
- Routes mouse and keyboard input with layer-aware hit testing and outside-click dismissal.
- Integrates with `WindowManager` for desktop window hierarchies.
popup.section.overview.body:
`Popup` represents a lightweight floating container anchored to a specific target widget or screen coordinate.

Key features:
- Anchor-based relative positioning (`TOP`, `BOTTOM`, `LEFT`, `RIGHT`).
- Boundary constraint checks against parent host bounds.
- Optional dismissal when clicking outside the popup boundaries (`closeOnOutsideClick`).
- State listeners for open and close events (`onOpenChanged`).
progress.bar.section.overview.body:
`ProgressBar` provides visual feedback on task completion through determinate percentage fills or indeterminate animated activity indicators.

Key features:
- Configurable value ranges with `min`, `max`, and current `value`.
- Smooth progress computation (`progress()`).
- Indeterminate mode for tasks with unknown completion time.
- Customizable track and indicator styling.
spinner.section.overview.body:
`Spinner` is a circular loading animation widget that visualizes continuous background processing.

Key features:
- Multiple presentation styles: segmented circular bars, dots, rings.
- Dynamic rotation speed, radius, arc count, and stroke thickness.
- Color customization for active and inactive segments.
toast.section.overview.body:
`Toast` provides transient, non-intrusive status messages that automatically disappear after a specified timeout.

Key features:
- Plain and rich-text message formatting.
- Configurable auto-dismiss duration and fade transitions.
- Optional status icon and custom actions.
- Stackable integration within `NotificationView`.
tooltip.section.overview.body:
`Tooltip` displays a floating helper box containing contextual information when a user hovers over an interactive UI element.

Key features:
- Plain text and RichText formatted layout.
- Automatic boundary detection to keep tooltip content within screen bounds.
- Show and hide delay thresholds to prevent accidental flickering.
- Customizable background, border, text color, and padding.
window.manager.section.overview.body:
`WindowManager` controls the lifecycle, z-ordering, focus stacking, and spatial positioning of floating desktop windows inside an `OverlayLayer`.

Key responsibilities:
- Window registration, activation, and focus management.
- Z-order stacking with `bringToFront` and `sendToBack`.
- Modal dialog stacking, preventing interaction with lower windows until the modal dialog is dismissed.
- Active window queries and window hierarchy iteration.
window.widget.section.overview.body:
`WindowWidget` is a full-featured desktop-style floating window container with title bar, window actions, dragging, resizing, collapse, modal dialogs, and docking system integrations.

Key capabilities:
- Title bar with plain-text or RichText titles, icons, and action buttons (minimize, collapse, close).
- 8-direction and corner resizing with configurable minimum size and resize grips.
- Boundary snapping and host constraints (`constrainToHost`).
- Modal mode support with background scrim dimming.
- Seamless docking integration with `DockingRoot` and `DockPane` docking trees.

map.canvas.section.overview.body:
`MapCanvas` is a high-level cartographic visualization widget built on top of `WorldCanvas`.

Key features:
- Map dimensions in dedicated map coordinates (`mapSize`, `mapWidth`, `mapHeight`).
- Texture and fallback color rendering with UV sub-region selection (`texture`, `source`).
- Coordinate grid and boundary outlines (`gridVisible`, `gridSize`, `mapBorderVisible`).
- Coordinate transformation between game world and map coordinates via `MapProjection`.
- Interactive marker management using `MapMarkerHandle` and `MapMarker`.
map.marker.section.overview.body:
`MapMarker` is a neutral base container widget for displaying map markers on a `MapCanvas`.

Key capabilities:
- Hosts arbitrary nested UI widgets or simple text labels (`content`, `label`).
- Built-in visual states for selection (`selected`) and target highlighting (`highlighted`).
- Unsurfaced transparent style by default for clean icon and label presentation.
- Governed by an underlying `AnchorWidget` for coordinate positioning.
map.marker.handle.section.overview.body:
`MapMarkerHandle` provides a fluent configuration handle for widgets added as markers to a `MapCanvas`.

Key features:
- Repositioning in map coordinates (`position`) or projected external world coordinates (`projectedPosition`).
- Fixed screen-space sizing with min/max zoom clamping (`screenSize`, `minScreenSize`, `maxScreenSize`).
- Dynamic zoom scaling relative to a reference zoom factor (`zoomScaling`).
- Normalized pivot point adjustment (`pivot`) and viewport culling (`cullOutsideViewport`).
- Zoom-level LOD visibility ranges (`visibleZoom`).
map.projection.section.overview.body:
`MapProjection` performs fast axis-aligned linear transformations between external game world coordinates and internal `MapCanvas` map coordinates.

Transformation model:
- `mapX = worldX * scaleX + offsetX`
- `mapY = worldY * scaleY + offsetY`

Calibration:
- Direct creation via explicit scale and offset values (`MapProjection(scaleX, offsetX, scaleY, offsetY)`).
- Calibration from two calibration point pairs using `MapProjection.axisAligned(...)` or the fluent builder `MapProjection.affine()`.
anchor.layer.section.overview.body:
`AnchorLayer` manages a collection of screen-space UI widgets pinned to world coordinates within a `WorldCanvas`.

Key responsibilities:
- Adding, looking up, and removing anchored widgets (`add`, `anchor`, `remove`, `clear`).
- Hosting interactive widgets (buttons, labels, panels) that maintain screen-space interactivity while following camera movement.
- Efficient snapshot caching for fast frame-by-frame rendering and event routing.
anchor.widget.section.overview.body:
`AnchorWidget` is the spatial controller for a UI widget pinned to a world coordinate position inside `WorldCanvas`.

Capabilities:
- World coordinate positioning (`worldPosition`, `worldX`, `worldY`).
- Screen-space dimensions independent of zoom (`screenSize`) or zoom-scaled sizing (`zoomScaling`).
- Min/max screen size clamping to prevent markers becoming unreadable at extreme zoom levels.
- Normalized pivot offset (`pivot`), visibility zoom range (`visibleZoomRange`), and off-screen viewport culling (`cullOutsideViewport`).
ribbon.layer.section.overview.body:
`RibbonLayer` renders continuous textured or solid ribbon lines, waypoint routes, and geometric paths within a `WorldCanvas`.

Key features:
- Textured or solid color ribbons with configurable world width and texture repeat distance (`width`, `textureLength`).
- Mesh caching: geometry is cached until points, camera viewport, or styling options change.
- Advanced styling via `RibbonOptions`: closed paths, miter limits, UV swapping/flipping, and rounded joint dots.
- Point list manipulation: `path`, `addPoint`, `clear`.
world.canvas.section.overview.body:
`WorldCanvas` is an infinite 2D/3D camera canvas that maps world coordinates into screen-space UI pixels.

Key capabilities:
- Interactive camera panning and zooming via mouse dragging and wheel scroll (`panningEnabled`, `zoomEnabled`, `wheelPanningEnabled`).
- Viewport models and camera bounds (`viewport`, `worldBounds`, `clampToWorldBounds`).
- Coordinate transformation utilities: `worldToRoot`, `rootToWorld`, `worldToLocal`, `localToWorld`.
- Layered architecture hosting background `WorldLayer` renderers underneath interactive `AnchorLayer` widgets.
world.layer.section.overview.body:
`WorldLayer` is a functional rendering interface for decorative, background, or data-driven visual layers inside `WorldCanvas`.

Usage:
- Ideal for coordinate grids, background terrain textures, route ribbons, heatmaps, and debug geometries.
- Invoked during the canvas rendering pass with access to the host `WorldCanvas` and `DrawScope`.
- Translates world coordinates to screen root coordinates using `canvas.worldToRootX()` and `canvas.worldToRootY()`.
